Transforms the wearer into a heavily armoured crab, fusing whatever body armour they are wearing into the shell and magnifying most of its benefits. In this form, they are slow-moving, but well-defended and even capable of wielding a two-handed weapon in their large main claw. Despite all this bulk, they are well-adapted to the water. They can also breathe clouds of rust at the cost of their own HP, which corrode and weaken enemies.

A copper and tungsten tambourine that vibrates excitedly in your hands, as if eager to be used. Just as music brings people together, shaking it with the proper rhythm will draw a large group of monsters into a narrow space and hold any hostile ones in place for a short time with inescapable waves of crushing gravity. The area of effect and duration increases with Evocations skill.

The dried remains of a tail shed under duress. Partially transforms the user into a hypnogecko, a reptile with a remarkable degree of metachrosis. Their skin naturally changes colour to blend in with their surroundings, making them stealthy, and when badly injured, they reflexively shed their own tail and make it scintillate with bright colours as a decoy - allowing them to either flee or even strike at their distracted predators from a blind spot.

A stone of unearthly beauty and almost immeasurable value outside the dungeon. Within its confines, it is utterly useless. Zot hoards these gems jealously, and will spitefully smash them soon after an adventurer enters the branch of the Dungeon in which they rest. Still, a very quick-moving adventurer might seize one first and keep its precious shards. Zot cannot track gems outside their home branches, so with truly astonishing speed, it might be possible to abscond with one still intact... but such a feat is difficult to credit, and likely pointless besides. Once the Orb of Zot is taken, Zot will be unable to smash any gems.
A giant lump of wood with sharp spikes at one end.
A pole with a large, heavy blade on one end.
The scales of a golden dragon. It is much heavier than most dragon scale armours, and grants its wearer resistance to poison, fire and cold.

A heavy stone icon, bearing the countenance of some long-forgotten king or god. Transforms the wearer into a slow, stone statue. The wearer's stone body is immune to poison and miasma, and gains resistance to electricity, negative energy, and torment. Shapeshifting skill increases armour granted.

A book describing how the mighty among summoners can bend to their will the terrible things from betwixt the planes. Many have been the unwary souls, however, who have toyed with this tome and been driven mad by unimaginable eldritch horrors.
An enormous metal war club, of great cumbrousness.
A sword with a very long, heavy blade and a long handle.
A collection of spells from great wizards throughout history. The author seems to have been extremely enthusiastic, and each wizard is described in voluminous, comprehensive detail.

A collection of spells from great wizards throughout history. The author seems to have been quite tired of their project - the wizards' descriptions are terse and minimal, meeting the lowest requirement for completeness.
A polearm consisting of an axe blade topped with a spike, mounted on a long shaft.
A blunt striking weapon, essentially equivalent to a mace.

A machine that fires metal slugs via applied thaumaturgy. Some enchant their projectiles to fall forward instead of down, others bewitch the slugs with a fatal attraction to their targets. All are slow, loud, and blast out thick smoke with each shot.
A practical introduction to Forgecraft, covering basic principles and their common applications.

A preserved and decorated hive, still dripping with ambrosial nectar. Transforms the wearer into a living beehive, filled with the buzz of countless insects labouring inside them. The nectar produced within greatly increases the wearer's health and magic regeneration and if they become seriously injured, angry bees will swarm out to defend their hive.

The horn belonging to Geryon, guardian of the Vestibule of Hell. It has the power to call forth demonic beasts. With high Evocations skill, it will call greater numbers of beasts, with lower chances of those beasts being hostile.
A piece of cloth and leather for launching stones, adequate for hunting small game like rabbits or goblins.
The scales of a cold-breathing dragon. It provides great protection from cold, while rendering its wearer more susceptible to fire.

A small bottle filled with mystical ink. Transforms the wearer into a walking scroll whose body is tattooed with the knowledge of a hundred mages. Being an omnibus of magical techniques gives them increased skill with all spell schools, which improves with Shapeshifting skill, but the form's ability to channel such magic is limited, and it cannot cast spells above level 4. Its attacks are also very weak, but have a chance of restoring 1 MP when they hit.
[[gem]] Countless spirits swirl around this gem, shrouding it in a bone-deep chill. Unwelcome in the Good gods' afterlife, they find here a heaven of their own.

[[gem]] Sigils of fire burn deep within this gem, symbol of the eternal compact between naga and salamander. Their bond is that of the poison which scourges the impure and the flame which burns away impurity.

A small statuette carved out of multi-hued jade which thrums with quiet power. Causes a great mantle of elementally-attuned crystal to grow out of the wearer's head and upper body, increasing their proficiency with fire, ice, earth, and air magic, but impairing all other schools. Each time the wearer casts a spell from one of those four schools, it will empower the corresponding crystal and unleash a burst of damaging magic. If all four crystals become charged at once, the wearer's resistances and fortitude will be temporarily enhanced.

A lightweight penetrating spear, designed for throwing. It will pass through the targets it hits, potentially hitting all targets in its path until it reaches maximum range. {{ if you.race() == "Kobold" or you.race() == "Spriggan" then return "Unfortunately, it is too long and awkward for you to use." end }}
A piece of wood and metal, to be strapped on one arm for defence.
A very rare and extremely effective weapon, featuring a pole with half-moon blades at both ends.
A very large and very heavy stone. {{ if you.race() == "Oni" or you.race() == "Troll" then return "" else return "Only large creatures are capable of throwing it." end }}
A suit made from layers of tanned animal hide. It provides basic protection with almost no hindrance to spellcasting or stealthy movement.

A rod that allows its wielder to fire unavoidable blasts of lightning. Consecutive evocations cause the discharge to be sustained, which increases the power level up to four times and allows the blast to be redirected to affect an area. The strength of the blast increases with Evocations skill and, for redirected blasts, decreases with the size of the affected area.

A painted eyepatch made from a scrap of wolf pelt. Transforms the wearer into a vicious werewolf, muscles surging with predatory instinct. Killing enemies with melee attacks in this form will give a stacking bonus to your damage and accuracy, and slaying enough of them in a row will cause you to unleash a vicious howl that makes any still alive cower in fear - and leaves them susceptible to a devastating leaping takedown.
A valuable book which allows one to learn a certain skill faster.

A loosely bound collection of the infamous Maxwell's schemes, diagrams and plans. Amidst messages written to and by his many minions, allies of convenience and hated rivals, a patient reader can discover spells of electrifying power.

A miniature, desiccated head of some ferocious and hopefully extinct creature. Transforms the wearer's midsection into a giant mouth, gnashing and ready to devour foes. This maw confers a powerful bite attack which scales additionally with the wearer's own strength and can devour slain creatures to temporariy increase one's regeneration. Unfortunately, it also confers such profound hunger that it can be difficult to pull oneself away from particularly appetising foes.

A fossilised jellyfish polyp, inscribed with sigils. Causes a mane of long stinging tendrils to sprout from the wearer's head which lash out at nearby enemies whenever the wearer attacks, poisoning them. When they feel their host's life is in danger, they can even turn these poisoned foes to stone.

[[gem]] The stoneborn brought forth this gem from the uttermost depths of the earth as a gift and a warning: beware Zot! That it lies now within Zot's power is a sure proof of the perversity of mortals and fate alike.

[[gem]] Smooth as a spider's silk, white as the eyes of some crawling thing which has lived too long in the dark, this gem buzzes with a fearful potential. Still, to a certain eye, it possesses a strange allure...

A small censer from which pours an endless smoky haze. Transforms the wearer's head into a billowing shroud of mist. Any potions they drink in this form will be rapidly decomposed into gases which they can expel via melee attacks as blasts of harmful clouds. They can also slowly condense the dungeon's air into potions of mist, allowing them to become intangible and blind monsters. However, the lack of typical mouth parts makes it difficult to pronounce incantations, greatly slowing the speed at which they cast spells.
A mace with a head covered in short spikes.

[[gem]] Though it drips with mud and muck, still a peculiar dignity attaches itself to this gem. The people of the Swamp, who first carried this stone, struggled against insurmountable odds. They failed, but there is much to admire even in the ruin of their efforts.

While purporting itself to be the personal account of a famous naturalist, it becomes clear upon reading that this book was compiled from multiple unrelated sources, including notes from a stagehand of a travelling magical circus. The travelogue may be fictitious, but some of the spell diagrams carefully transcribed in the margins seem quite real.
An extremely rare book, powerful and sinister. Many foolhardy magicians have tried to study this tome, only to find themselves entangled within necromantic forces they could not hope to control.
A sphere of crystal, carried in place of a shield. Magic scintillates within its interior.
An invaluable artefact. Once you have escaped to the surface with it, your quest is complete.
A recurved bow, crudely crafted from troll-bone and warg hair. The cave orcs' use of archery, so unlike their surface-dwelling ancestors, shows the influence of their elvish allies.
A pair of boots. They are worn on the feet, and cover all but the largest hooves and talons.
A pair of gloves. They are worn on the hands, and cover all but the largest claws.
A brief text on magic, perhaps excerpted from some larger work. It contains knowledge of one spell.
A long polearm with sharp protrusions on either side of the spearhead.
The nacreous scales of a pearl dragon. It grants its wearer resistance to negative energies.

A hand mirror which can create a reflection of a nearby creature, clouding in the process. The reflection's duration increases with Evocations skill and decreases with the willpower of the target. It is, invariably, slightly weaker than the creature it mirrors.

An enchanted vessel of elemental water. Removing the stopper unleashes a torrent of water, smashing the target and flooding the nearby area. If any creatures engulfed by the wave need air to breathe, they'll be unable to cast spells until they recover. The strength of the torrent and the duration of the flooding increase with Evocations skill.
A full suit of solid metal plate: cuirass, pauldrons, vambraces, waist plate and greaves. It provides excellent protection.

A strange substance, produced by ghost moths. Consuming it causes regeneration of health and magic, along with total befuddlement. The two effects are fundamentally linked – the regeneration ends the moment the confusion does.

A potion which can send one into an incoherent rage, granting them a great but temporary increase to their health, damage, and speed. In exchange, their mind is clouded by anger, only allowing them to move and attack in melee. The rage will wear off quickly if they do not attack monsters, and upon expiry, the imbiber will be fatigued, causing them to slow dramatically and rendering them unable to berserk again for a short duration.

A potion which grants the imbiber both great sagacity and great impatience, fully restoring their magic and making them brilliant, but shortly thereafter sending them into an incoherent rage that prevents all spellcasting.
A potion which increases the power of the drinker's spells and halves their magic cost (rounding up).
A potion which ends most magical effects, good or bad, affecting one who drinks it. It also reduces magical contamination.
A potion which restores a small amount of health, and cures poison and confusion.
A potion which uplifts both the body and mind of its drinkers, lifting them from the ground and increasing their Will to resist the world's temptations.
A bitter liquid which makes the imbiber extremely efficient at engaging enemies for a short while, causing a single movement to close any distance - whether they'd like it to or not.
A truly wonderful and very rare drink, which grants experience when consumed.
An enchanted beverage which speeds the actions of anyone who drinks it.
A magical healing elixir which causes wounds to close and heal almost instantly.
A potion which confers invisibility on one who consumes it. [[player invis desc]]

While invisible, most monsters have greatly reduced accuracy against you, cannot make attacks of opportunity, and the spells they cast may sometimes be aimed at the wrong location. They may also stumble around and eventually lose track of you, especially if their intelligence is low. In addition, melee attacks you make against such creatures have a chance (proportional to your stealth and weapon skill) of catching them off-guard and dealing increased damage, especially if performed with a short blade. Certain creatures can see through this invisibility and it will always be completely ineffective while standing in water.

A potion which transforms the imbiber into an animated banyan tree, with sap for blood and branches capable of holding weapons. Such a tree has minimal evasion but increased health and natural armour, and is resistant to poison, and immune to negative energy, torment, sleep, blinding, and does not need to breathe. However, it is rooted in place while the transformation lasts, and cannot teleport.
A valuable potion which grants an infusion of magical energy.
A potion which greatly increases the power of the drinker's melee attacks.

A vial of mist which temporarily turns the imbiber's body insubstantial, protecting them from constriction, petrification, barbs, sticky flame, webs, nets, and being caught by bolas. It will also end most of those effects if they are already afflicted.
A potent alcohol, distilled in some dubious corner of the dungeon. Drinking it reduces the imbiber's accuracy, evasion, and spellcasting success for a while.
A potion which mutates the drinker, removing several mutations then granting a few random mutations, which are likely (but not guaranteed) to be beneficial.
A potion which grants temporary resistance to a variety of harmful effects: fire, cold, electricity, poison, and acid.

A potion which makes the drinker attract enemies, translocating them quickly closer for the duration of the effect. The effect is surprisingly subtle, and unwary victims may sleep through it entirely.
[[gem]] Shining with every colour of the rainbow and a few others besides, some consider this gem 'a bit tacky'. Preposterous!

An ever-changing fragment of something primordial; its substance seems to undulate between flesh and bone and perhaps even metal. A sufficiently skilled shapeshifter can stabilise it into a useable - if unpredictable - form. (If your Shapeshifting skill is at least 6, attempting to put this on will transform it into a random one of: Rimehorn, Scarab, Medusa, or Spore talismans.)
A mysterious item resembling a rune of some kind. Once evoked, it will make the user glow blue and add a reverb to all sound... and there may be other effects as well.
A sturdy wooden pole, meant for fighting.

The scales of a quicksilver dragon. Although it does not provide its wearer with as much protection as the scales of some heavier dragons, it is somewhat lighter and less encumbering. The armour repels both attacks on the wearer's willpower and magical modification of itself - it cannot be enchanted.
A dagger with an uncanny enchantment upon it, allowing it to strike twice for every blow its wielder makes. It takes great skill to use to its full potential.
A spiny trinket reminiscent of a cactus. Causes sharp quills to grow all over the wearer's body which may cause injury to anyone unwise enough to attack them in melee.
A slender, sharply pointed sword, with an uncommonly elegant design.

An intricate puzzlebox containing an unknowable prize. Transforms the wearer into a riddle-loving sphinx. In this form, they are {{ if you.race() == "Felid" then return "normally capable of wearing a cloak and barding (though your" .. " own diminutive size would prevent this)" else return "capable of wearing a cloak and barding" end }}, and their melee attacks cause powerful winds to strike their foe which do increased damage for every open space next to them. They are also masterful enchanters, casting Hex spells much more easily and ignoring a portion of their foe's Willpower. Alas, their love of riddles is so compulsive that even the most hardened adventurer will be unable to resist posing them to new foes they encounter, no matter how unwise this may be.

A crude ornament carved from the horn of a rare arctic beast - so cold to the touch that ice still clings to it. Transforms the wearer into a rime yak, a hardy ungulate that is highly resistant to cold and whose breath is so frigid that it freezes the walls around itself as it fights. Being so attuned to arctic temperatures also makes it easier for the wearer to cast Ice magic.
A light leather suit reinforced with a covering of metal rings. It is protective in combat, but slightly uncomfortable due to the added weight.
A ring that increases the dexterity of its wearer.
A ring that makes its wearer more capable of avoiding attacks.
A ring that increases the intelligence of its wearer.
A ring that protects its wearer from the effects of acid and corrosion.
A ring that increases its wearer's reserves of magical power for so long as it is worn.
A ring that protects its wearer from poison.
A ring that protects its wearer from the effects of negative energy.
A ring that protects its wearer from most sources of damage.
A ring that protects its wearer from cold.
A ring that protects its wearer from fire.
A ring that increases its wearer's willpower, protecting against certain magical effects.
A ring that allows its wearer to see invisible things.
A ring that increases the wearer's accuracy and damage with ranged weapons and melee attacks.
A ring that increases the strength of its wearer.
A ring that increases the success rate of its wearer's magical spells.
A large, loose-fitting, wide-sleeved outer garment made of light cloth. It offers little protection against physical harm, but does not hinder evasion or spellcasting.
A charm which allows entry into the Realm of Zot.
A woven silk bag. Opening it will cover the area with webs, spiders, and other skittering things. Evocations skill increases spider quality, quantity and webbing.
A blessed weapon, woven by the saints in Heaven and hated by the unholy. It is a favoured weapon of the Shining One's servants.

A vial of roiling blood that pulses with the beat of an unseen heart. Transforms the wearer into a fearsome vampire - a creature that straddles the border between life and undeath. They can drink the lifeblood of the living to heal themselves, and even turn those they slay stealthily into vampiric thralls, but do not heal in the presence of monsters. Their hypnotic gaze often prevents monsters from shouting when alerted and may even daze them. At great effort, they can also scatter into a swarm of bats - either to flee or to assail their enemies.

[[gem]] They who smote down Death herself and buried themselves in a Tomb of their own making were not shy of their ambitions. Fain to seize upon baubles and overweening proud, their Lord journeyed into their eternal unrest with this gem upon their breast.
A leather suit covered with metal plates attached to each other in overlapping rows to provide full protection, but at the cost of reduced freedom of movement.

A small golden cameo of a beetle. Transforms the wearer into a sun scarab, a fiery insect that carries around a mote of searing heat and light outside itself, like a tiny sun. This solar ember burns adjacent enemies whenever the scarab attacks, and can be healed by swapping with it. In addition, the scarab's own mandibles can reduce enemies' fire resistance and Fire spells are easier for the wearer to cast.
A length of stylish fabric. At its creation, enchantments were woven into it, and as such it cannot accept further enchantment.

A wonderful scroll which causes the creation of a valuable item, with the reader choosing from a small selection. The items offered will often be a good match for the reader's skills; and if nothing recommends itself, the reader can always choose a heap of gold.
A scroll that allows its reader to selectively erase one spell from memory to recapture the magical energy bound up with it.
A scroll that allows its reader to teleport a short distance, with precise control.

A scroll that imbues a weapon with a random brand. Any existing brand will be replaced with a different one, and any brand forbidden by your current god will not be chosen. Artefacts cannot be branded in this way. Melee weapons will commonly be branded with the flaming, freezing, heavy, venom or protection brand (or with the special brand exclusive to the category of weapon being branded), and rarely with the draining, electrocution, spectral, vampiric or chaos brand. Ranged weapons will commonly be branded with the flaming, freezing, heavy or draining brand, and rarely with the electrocution or chaos brand.
A scroll that surrounds its user with a flight of beautiful butterflies, blowing back other creatures nearby with the flapping of their wings.

A scroll that places an enchantment on a piece of armour chosen by the reader. Body armour and bardings can be enchanted up to the same value as their base armour rating. Bucklers, kite shields and tower shields can be enchanted up to +3, +5 or +8 respectively, and other armour can be enchanted up to +2. Magical artefacts cannot be enchanted at all.
A scroll that places an enchantment on a weapon chosen by the reader, increasing both accuracy and damage. Weapons can be enchanted up to +9. Magical artefacts cannot be enchanted at all.

A scroll that causes great fear in nearby foes, causing them to flee until attacked, cornered, or enough time has passed. Non-living, undead and plant monsters cannot be feared, and berserk or frenzied monsters are also immune.
A scroll that surrounds the reader with a dense cloud of fog, which can block vision temporarily. The fog takes a short time to fully spill out.
A scroll that summons a small amphibian companion for a short time.
A useful magic scroll which identifies the properties of any unknown object.

A scroll that fills the creatures around the reader with an unstable and powerful inner flame. This fire is released any time the victims are hit, and explosively released upon their death. Giant creatures cause bigger explosions.
A prank scroll that creates a loud noise when read.

A scroll that causes a flurry of pebbles to continuously pelt nearby ceatures over several turns, doing minimal damage. As the effect ends, slightly more unusual detritus may be thrown at them, impairing or distracting them in some way for a short period of time.
A scroll that fills the air with poison, covering every unoccupied space in sight with toxic fumes.

A scroll that reveals its reader's surroundings. The layout of the current floor is fully mapped, and everything within a moderate radius, including both visible and invisible monsters, is momentarily shown.

A scroll that eliminates all sound near the reader. This makes reading scrolls, casting spells, invoking divine abilities, or shouting impossible in the reader's vicinity. Certain monsters have innate magical or special abilities which will still be usable while silenced. The effect starts out with a large radius, which will then shrink, eventually covering only the reader, before it times out.
A scroll that calls forth several allied creatures woven from shadow into the shapes of those beings found within the reader's immediate vicinity.
A scroll that translocates the reader to a random position after a short delay. Reading this scroll while waiting for a teleportation will instead cancel it.

A scroll that calls on the powers of darkness to inflict great pain on any nearby creature — including the reader! This halves the resilience of all living creatures and cuts down all holy creature resilence by about a third, although it is never directly fatal.
A scroll that briefly halves the willpower of the reader and any nearby beings, rendering them vulnerable to many magical effects. The scroll cannot affect those fully immune to such effects.
A farm implement, usually only used by untrained mobs in combat. In practice, it's quite similar to a halberd.

A jade snake coiled around a fossilised egg. Transforms the wearer into an amphisbaena - a legendary two-headed serpent. It is capable of wearing two pieces of headgear at once and its powerful coils can wind around foes and crush them to death, but its cold blood leaves it susceptible to being slowed by cold attacks.

[[gem]] Many are the treasures of the Ironbound Order, but none older nor more precious than this steel-shining gem. The Vaults were first forged to hold it, and none who gazed within its depths could fault the choice.

[[gem]] Unearthly energies gently flow along the surface of this gem, guided by the archmage who first built the Elven Halls. Countless generations of elves flocked to learn from her, but her foremost pursuit was always the perfection of this piece of art.

A coupon good for one item of any price from any store in the dungeon, to be used automatically when you would make a purchase that exceeds your funds. How generous! No refunds. One coupon per purchase per customer. Offer limited by availability. Void if defaced or otherwise altered. Valid only within the dungeon of Zot and its subsidiary branches. Additional purchase not required.
A curved piece of wood and string, for shooting arrows.
A personal stabbing weapon with a short grip.

[[gem]] Swirls of dark smoke seem to lurk in the depths of this gem. Countless dark deeds were done in the Dungeon even before Zot seized and remade it, and their dreadful residue now taints every hint of beauty trapped within its confines.
A hunting weapon consisting of a wooden shaft with a pointed metal head fastened on one end.

A strange charm made from shed arachnid exoskeletons bound together with silk. Transforms the wearer into an agile jumping spider who can move swiftly towards foes and inflict grievous damage on any it catches unaware. It cannot be ensnared by webs, but its attacks can ensnare its enemies in them. It can also leap briskly away from many dangers.

A small charm made from a still-living mushroom. Transforms one of the wearer's arms and parts of their lower body into a vibrant mass of multicoloured fungus. Melee attacks in this form may release spores that weaken their target, as well as cause mushrooms to sprout on the ground behind them which will release their own bursts of dazing spores if allowed to grow. Shapeshifting skill increases the durability of these mushrooms as well as their damage.

A staff that increases the power of air spells cast by its wielder, and insulates them from electricity. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Air Magic, they can shock those struck by it, dealing electrical damage which bypasses half of defenders' armour.

A staff that increases the power of alchemy spells cast by its wielder, and protects them from the effects of poison. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Alchemy, they can envenom those struck by it.

A staff that increases the power of ice spells cast by its wielder, and protects them from the effects of cold. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Ice Magic, they can freeze those struck by it.
A staff that increases the power of conjurations cast by its wielder. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Conjurations, they can blast those they strike with pure energy.

A staff that increases the power of necromantic spells cast by its wielder, and protects them from negative energy. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Necromancy, they can inflict great pain on those living souls they strike, dealing negative energy damage which bypasses armour.

A staff that increases the power of earth spells cast by its wielder. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Earth magic, they can fracture the ground beneath those struck by it, dealing substantial damage - though much less to creatures which fly.

A staff that increases the power of fire spells cast by its wielder, and protects them from the effects of fire. If the wielder is skilled in Evocations and Fire Magic, they can burn those struck by it.
[[gem]] Odd lights twinkle within the depths of this gem. From what strange stuff is it made, and from what distant land did it travel?

The scales of a steam-breathing dragon. Unlike the scales of some larger dragons, it does not provide its wearer with much protection (beyond a resistance to scalding steam), but it is extremely light and supple.
A small chunk of dense but otherwise unremarkable natural mineral. It can be thrown to cause minor damage.
The scales of a great umbral dragon. It is heavier than most dragon scale armours, but its encumbrance does not penalise the wearer's stealth. It also grants additional stealth to the wearer.
The scales of a lightning-breathing dragon. It is heavier than most dragon scale armours, and gives its wearer resistance to electrical discharges.

Lightning trapped, impossibly, in a bottle. Lets the wearer walk through the air as a raging, lightning-filled tempest. The wearer's melee attacks are electrified and strike all adjacent foes. The wearer also flies, gains immunity to poison, miasma, petrification, constriction, and sticky flame, and also resists electricity. They can launch themselves as a lightning bolt, blasting through everything in their way.
The scales of a swamp dragon. It confers resistance to poison on its wearer.

A grey-black vessel, infused with dark power through a sickening ritual. Transforms the wearer into an undying offence against life itself. Foes struck by wearer's melee weapons or hands are weakened, slowed, and drained. The wearer can also heal themself by tormenting living foes nearby; Shapeshifting skill increases the amount healed. Further, the wearer resists cold, has enhanced willpower, and is immune to poison, miasma, negative energy, and torment. The wearer also gains some of the more dubious benefits of having an undead body. They are vulnerable to holy damage and Dispel Undead, and cannot consume potions.

A compilation of children's stories about great adventures, always ending with the traveller returning to the place they started. The love infused into its pages by countless generations has granted it power, allowing a skilled mage to transport others by reciting specific passages.
A mesh of ropes knotted together with weights around the edge, used to entangle and entrap targets. Struggling victims can eventually destroy the net and break free, if they live long enough.
A large piece of wood and metal, to be strapped on one arm for defence.

A set of dormant, magnetic earth elementals in the form of tiny, very heavy pebbles. When released, the elementals are drawn magnetically to the center of nearby monsters, where they literally explode with rage at their rest being disturbed. Tremorstones usually land slightly off-target, and the user is always at risk of being hit. However, armour is extremely effective at repelling the lightweight fragments of rock from a tremorstone's explosion, so a well-armoured wielder has little to fear. Evocations skill increases the number of explosions.

An analytical volume discussing methods and materials with which to construct a dizzying array of traps - from those intended to safeguard a pantry from ants to ones which would please even the most sadistic dungeon architect.
A fishing spear improved with a longer shaft and a three-pronged metal head.
A magical book written by a numerologically obsessed wizard. Everything from sentence length to overall organization is structured. It's unclear whether the author thought this was helpful.
A crossbow with three strings arranged in series to provide exceptional power, initially designed as a siege weapon and then scaled down. It takes a considerable amount of time to load and fire.
A formidable weapon created by a master craftsman. The blade of the sword forks into three great razor-sharp edges.
A blessed trident moulded by cleansing flame, with three points symbolising the combined might of the three holy gods. It is a favoured weapon of the Shining One's servants.
The stiff and knobbly skin of a troll. It magically regenerates its wearer's flesh, once attuned to the wearer's body at full health.
A collection of spells that assault everything in sight of the caster, unrestrained by petty limitations like 'needing a clear shot' or 'concern about collateral damage'.

A small charm bearing the likeness of an eye. It gives the wearer supernatural sight, allowing them to perceive the clouds of magical residue left behind whenever beings cast spells. Touching those clouds allows them to convert that leftover magic into unnerring projectiles against nearby foes. This third eye even allows one to see from further distances than would otherwise be possible{{ if you.get_base_mutation_level("+LOS") > 0 then return " (but your own vision is already as long as possible)." else return ", but be warned - creatures perceived this way will perceive you back." end }}
A magical device which throws bolts of corrosive acid.
A magical device which causes a creature to become fiercely, but briefly, loyal to the user.
A magical device which drills tunnels through unworked rock.
A magical device which throws little puffs of flame.
A magical device which creates a loud explosion of ice shards, bypassing half of victims' resistance to cold.

A magical device which fires a ray of searing light, injuring and blinding those struck. Only living, undead, demonic and angelic monsters can be blinded, and tougher monsters will recover their vision more quickly.

A magical device which launches a psychic attack on a target creature. If it overcomes their willpower, it 'blows their mind' in a violently literal fashion, dealing damage that bypasses their armour entirely. It is useless against mindless creatures.
A magical device which can render a creature immobile, incapable of moving any of its limbs.
A magical device which causes a creature to be transmogrified into another form. It is especially effective against shape-changing creatures.
A magical device which fires a beam of destructive energy, dispelling enchantments on creatures struck.

A magical device which fires a magical seed, entangling its target and adjacent foes in quick-growing tree roots. Those entangled will be immobilised and take damage over time until they escape or the roots wither away. The roots will only sprout from solid ground.
A magical device which creates a brief but violent rift in space, damaging everything caught in its wake and sometimes blinking them a short distance away.
A military axe with a long haft and a single-bladed head.

A small amphora from which pours a seemingly unending quantity of water. Transforms the wearer's flesh into elemental water, allowing them to move flexibly and reach to attack from a great distance, though without the precision needed to stab from range. From time to time, they can even cause the water around them to rise up and drown their enemies. The malleability of this water preserves most other aspects of the wearer's physiology such as their blood and bones, and even allows them to retain the benefits of their physical mutations, but cold attacks can freeze it solid and fire may cause it to erupt with steam.
A long plaited strip of leather. Originally developed for use in disagreements with cattle, this simple weapon is now widely used to settle differences between all sorts of creatures.
An introductory book for the magic arts of poison. Readers are recommended to wear a pair of very thick, non-absorbent gloves.
You have detected an object here, but you do not know what it is.
This creature has temporarily gained the ability to cast specific spells. It will lose access to them again once sufficiently injured.
After a short delay, this creature will be teleported to somewhere else on the current floor.

This creature suffers AC-ignoring cold damage every turn, and may sometimes explode in a burst of ice that damages nearby allies. When it dies, it may spread rimeblight to other nearby allies. Natural, demonic, or holy creatures will be instantly killed once they reach low health, and be replaced with pillars of rime.
This creature is being targeted by one or more of your allies.
When this creature deals damage, it will suffer damage equal to the damage it dealt.

This creature is unable to move, act, block, or dodge. Any hostile action will awaken it, though melee attacks against it (even by other monsters) will deal increased damage. [[high-tier stab monstatus]]

This creature has 50% more health, deals 50% more damage with melee attacks, and both moves and acts 50% faster. They cannot perform any action besides moving or attacking. When the berserk rage wears off, they will be slowed and unable to berserk for a short duration.

This creature cannot see properly. Its accuracy is greatly decreased, it cannot make attacks of opportunity, and spells it casts may sometimes be aimed at the wrong locations. It may also stumble around and eventually lose track of its target, especially if it has low intelligence. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature cannot move under its own power, but may still use translocations or be forcibly displaced by someone else.
This monster has been called from a parallel reality. Killing it will grant no experience points, but it will be immediately cast back to its original reality as soon as the tesseract is destroyed.
This creature has used a breath ability recently and cannot use it again for a short while.

This creature is chanting a Word of Recall. This will recall intelligent allies from elsewhere on the floor to the caster's vicinity after a short delay, but can be interrupted by most effects which would normally prevent it from casting spells.
This creature has been charmed and will fight for your cause for a short while. This effect will wear off immediately if you attempt to harm it in any way.
This creature's natural venom has been intensified, giving any poison it inflicts through attacks or breath weapons a chance to slow and asphyxiate susceptible targets.

This creature is unable to block or use spells or abilities and will stumble around at random, attacking whatever it bumps into - be they friend or foe or sometimes even themselves. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature has been contaminated by transmutational energy, and will suffer significant damage every third time such energy is inflicted upon them.

This creature is being constricted by tree roots, which reduces their evasion and inflicts some damage each turn. It may also prevent them from moving, though each attempt to do so has a chance to break this effect entirely.

This creature is being constricted by clutching corpses from deep beneath the earth, which reduces their evasion and inflicts some damage each turn. It may also prevent them from moving, though each attempt to do so has a chance to break this effect entirely.
This formerly-friendly creature has been charmed by another creature to join their side. If you slay the source of this charm, it will regain its senses.

This creature has been coated in sticky flame, and will take AC-ignoring fire damage each turn. Movement will shake off the flames, causing it to expire much more rapidly and stepping into water will extinguish it entirely.

This creature is unable to evade attacks or turn invisible. If it dies, it will leave behind a cloud of magnetised fragments. Each time Magnavolt is cast, a beam of electricity will automatically be fired at this creature.
This creature has been afflicted with illusory wounds by a flayed ghost. These wounds will disappear with time or when the flayed ghost is destroyed.
This creature is stuck in liquefied ground, causing it to move more slowly and also fumble 25% of the melee attacks it makes.
This creature will be automatically destroyed in a few turns.
cursed with the promise of agony
This creature is cursed, and will lose half its current health after the next time the source of the curse hits it with a melee attack.
This creature is temporarily unable to act, but any hostile action will cause it to immediately regain its senses.
This creature has +24 EV when dodging projectiles, whether physical or magical.
This creature's spells are less powerful - dealing less damage, being less able to overcome their target's willpower, and occasionally being weaker in other ways.

This creature is protected by a divine shield which will unerringly block the next several blockable assaults before dissipating. All blocked projectiles will be reflected and melee attackers may be blinded by light.
This monster's current and maximum health are temporarily doubled.
empowered by the touch of Beogh

This creature has been granted great power by Beogh to challenge you. Their melee and ranged attacks deal 33% more damage, their health is increased, and they cast spells more frequently. They are also able to track you, no matter where on the current floor you flee. They will lose these bonuses once the challenge is concluded.
This creature has been flash-frozen and its movement speed is greatly reduced for a short time.

This creature is caught in a net, greatly reducing its evasion and preventing it from blocking. Any attempt it makes to move or attack will instead struggle against the net, which may eventually destroy it. Spellcasting is unimpaired. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]

This creature is caught in a spider's web, greatly reducing its evasion and preventing it from blocking. Any attempt it makes to move or attack will instead struggle against the web, which may eventually destroy it. Spellcasting is unimpaired. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature takes increased damage from all non-attack sources (except poison), non-attack projectiles are more accurate against them, and their Willpower is mildly reduced.
This creature suffers poison damage every turn and cannot be poisoned any further.
This creature is but a fragile duplicate of another creature. Its health is reduced by 66%, it deals 33% less damage with attacks, and its spells are significantly weakened.
This creature has been empowered by the flames of Ignis. It deals additional fire damage with its melee attacks, moves 33% more quickly, and has increased AC and resistance to fire.

This creature is fleeing in fear and will attempt each turn to move away from the source of this fear. Beside movement, it may only cast spells which it thinks could help it escape, such as Blink. If harmed directly or cornered against terrain, it will turn around to fight once more.
This creature receives 50% more damage from all sources.

This creature deals 50% more damage with melee attacks and both moves and attacks 50% faster. It cannot cast spells and will prioritise attacking the closest other creature present each turn, whether they are friend or foe.
This creature has gathered all the power it needs to cast its spells.
This creature has been struck with a kinetic grapnel. The next melee attack from the grapnel's source will always hit and deal slightly increased damage.
This creature has been heavily drained, lowering the accuracy of their melee attacks, the power of their spells and special attack properties, and making them more vulnerable to many status effects.
This creature has glows with the perfection of their best self. They deal 100% more damage with melee attacks, have additional AC, and cast spells with substantially more strength.

This creature has been blessed with great speed and power by the wrath of Gozag Ym Sagoz. Their haste, berserk, and empowered spells statuses are permanent and will not wear off with time or through deliberate magical intervention.
This creature is neither hostile nor allied and may attack creatures of all dispositions, should it wander into them.
This creature is infested with a death scarab, which will emerge from their body once they die.

Whenever this creature suffers damage, a flame cloud will briefly appear beneath them. When they die, they will explode in a violent burst of fire, damaging anything nearby and leaving behind additional flame clouds. Giant creatures will trigger an even larger explosion when they die.

You are currently terrified of this creature, preventing you from deliberately moving close to them and causing 33% of the melee attacks you make again against them fail. This effect will break if you ever lose sight of this creature.
This creature's melee attacks may inflict additional damage of a random element or cause various irresistible status effects.

This creature has been magically vexed and is forced to attack a random adjacent space each turn instead of performing any other actions. It is more likely to attack a space containing a creature than an empty one, but will attack its own allies as readily as its enemies.

This creature has been lightly drained, somewhat lowering the accuracy of their melee attacks, the power of their spells and special attack properties, and making them slightly more vulnerable to many status effects.

This creature has been driven to madness by the power of Zin. It will never again use spells or abilities and will stumble around at random, attacking whatever it bumps into - be they friend or foe or sometimes even themselves.
This creature's spells and magical abilities have been disrupted and may fail when used. The chance of failure depends on the remaining duration of this effect.
This creature has had its access to magic tainted. Whenever it casts a spell, its magic will be severely disrupted, making it likely any subsequent spells it casts will fail.
marked with the sign of ruin
This creature has been condemned to inexorable decay and ruin. Whenever it takes damage from melee attacks, it will be drained heavily and either slowed, weakened, or blinded.
This monster may be an illusion, having greatly reduced health and doing very little damage. Only one of them is real, and killing the original will destroy all the copies.
This creature has mesmerised you, making you unable to voluntarily move away from them. This effect will break if you ever lose sight of this creature.
This creature has been created by magic and will cease to be once its creator dies.
This creature's shadow has been torn away from it and cannot be affected by Aphotic Marionette ever again.
This creature's AC is reduced by 8 and its accuracy, spell power, brand damage, and willpower are moderately reduced.
This creature's fire resistance is reduced by one level.
This creature's poison resistance is reduced by one level.
This creature has been stricken permanently mute by the power of Zin. This prevents all noise the creature could make, including the vocalisations required for most creatures to cast spells.
This creature has been briefly distracted by something else. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature is slightly out of phase and has greatly increased evasion against those who lack the ability to see invisible creatures. Their degree of injury is also hidden.
This creature is unable to move, act, block, or dodge attacks. [[high-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature has built up part of the charge it needs to cast a spell or activate an ability.
This creature will never attack you and may attack other creatures hostile to you, but will neither follow you nor obey any direct instructions.
This creature will soon become fully petrified. Its movement and actions are 50% slower and it is nearly unable to dodge attacks, though it also takes 33% less damage. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]

This creature is unable to move, act, block, or dodge attacks. By being made of stone, it also takes 50% less damage, gains immunity to negative energy and poison, but become vulnerable to deconstruction. [[high-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature suffers poison damage every turn.

This creature is surrounded by a field of unnatural silence which eliminates all noise made within it as well as preventing the vocalisations required for many creatures (including you) to read scrolls, cast spells, or invoke divine aid. If this effect was caused by a spell, the radius of the field will shrink over time.
This creature shines with Olgreb's Toxic Radiance and will continuously inflict poison damage on all foes in sight for several turns.
This creature has been defeated in honourable combat and may be recruited as one of your apostles via the ability menu.
This creature has not yet inflicted you with Oblivion Howl and may attempt to do so.
This creature's Sundering weapon is fully charged and its next attack will be more accurate, inflict greatly increased damage, and cleave with increased range. This effect will be lost if it moves.
This creature reflects any projectile it blocks back to their original source.
Whenever this creature suffers damage, it inflicts 2/3rds as much damage back upon whatever damaged it.
This creature regenerates health at a greatly increased rate, proportion to their maximum health.
This creature has been ordered to flee in a given direction, and will not attack or return to your side until they are given new instructions or have travelled a sufficient distance
This creature has curled into a ball, increasing its movement speed and melee damage by 100% until the next time it attacks something (or becomes unable to move).
This creature will inflict a portion of all damage it suffers upon nearby allies, with those closer to it receiving a greater amount.
Half of the damage suffered by this creature is redirected to the ally protecting it instead.
This creature is sick and cannot naturally regenerate.
This creature is engulfed in a field of unnatural silence, preventing any noise it might make, including the vocalisations required for many creatures to cast spells.
This creature will take minor damage whenever it moves.
This creature is normally invisible, but your magical sight allows you to see it nonetheless. This has no effect on you, though any allies you have may not be able to see it as you can.
This creature moves and acts at 66% of normal speed.
This creature has been outlined with a halo of light and is easier to hit and revealed, if invisible.
This creature's soul has been bound in ice. When it dies, a simulacrum of its original form will rise in its place.
This creature's soul will be bound in service to you once they die, though allowing them to stray from your line of sight for more than a brief moment will cause you to lose your grasp on it.
A fragment of this creature's soul has been extracted into a soul wisp, preventing further use of this spell until the wisp reunites with them again.
This creature's spells are strengthened and it will cast them more frequently.
This creature's spells are significantly weakened.
This creature is preventing any clouds from being created on the current floor.
This creature is moving in a single direction at incredible speed. Any enemies they run into will be pushed backwards and attacked with 50% bonus damage and increased accuracy.
This creature's melee attacks deal 50% more damage.
This creature's willpower is increased by 2 pips.
This creature has been struck dumb by the power of Zin and cannot act. [[high-tier stab monstatus]]
This creature is the source of a devastating polar vortex.
This creature trails a ring of acidic fog clouds around itself.
This creature trails a ring of seething chaos clouds around itself.
This creature trails a ring of flame clouds around itself.
This creature trails a ring of purple smoke around itself.
This creature trails a ring of foul miasma around itself.
This creature trails a ring of freezing clouds around itself.
This creature trails a ring of mutagenic fog around itself.
This creature trails a ring of clouds of excruciating misery around itself.
This creature has recently cast Polar Vortex and cannot cast it again for a short time.
This creature trails a ring of thunder clouds around itself.
This creature has contributed to the death of one of your apostles. Defeating all targets of orcish vengeance will significantly speed up the time it takes for Beogh to resurrect your apostles.
Whenever you perform a ranged attack aimed at a different creature, a copy of the projectile will be teleported to this creature at the end of its flight.
This creature's melee attacks deal 25% more damage, its accuracy is slightly increased, and its spells and abilities have been mildly strengthened.
This creature has become unmoored in space, allowing it to Manifold Assault as a natural ability. Whenever they do, there is 33% chance they will also blink to a random nearby location.

This creature is unable to see you because you are invisible. Its accuracy against you is greatly decreased, it cannot make attacks of opportunity, and spells it casts may sometimes be aimed at the wrong locations. It may also stumble around and eventually lose track of you, especially if it has low intelligence. [[low-tier stab monstatus]]
Despite being engulfed in unnatural silence, this creature's magic does not require vocalisations and thus is unaffected.
This creature provides no experience or piety when slain.
Each turn, this creature blinks a short distance further away from you and suffers a small amount of damage.
This creature's evasion is slightly increased.
This creature's resistance to fire, cold, poison, electricity, and corrosion are all increased by one level.
This creature is poisoned and will take damage every turn.
This creature is unable to breathe and cannot cast spells or invoke divine aid. It also takes minor asphyxiation damage every turn.

This creature takes no damage by any means unless the original source of that damage is adjacent to them. Non-damaging side-effects happen normally. (The source of damage from clouds and projectile-like monsters, such as foxfires, is always considered whatever creature first created them.)
This creature's melee attacks deal 33% less damage.
This creature's willpower is reduced by half.
This creature is preparing to launch a clockwork bee and must focus on this task for several turns. Most effects that would prevent this creature from casting spells will also interrupt this process.
Your innate bond with this monster allows you to shoot through it and also protects it from any harm you might do to it.

<blue>Melee attacks you make against this creature have a chance (proportional to your stealth and weapon skill) of catching it off-guard and dealing increased damage, especially if made with a short blade.</blue>
<blue>Melee attacks you make against this creature will deal greatly increased damage, especially if made with a short blade.</blue>

This spriggan is aged and weathered from years of travel away from the forests and swamps that are home to her kin. Her choice of weapon and astonishing speed both speak to the training she underwent. Underestimate her at your peril!

Once the primary guardian serpent of a legendary treasure hoard, she was disgraced after thieves looted it while she slept. She seeks to make up for her failure by protecting the only treasure the villains overlooked, a single precious talisman.

Amaemon always knew he was different, but it was still a horrific surprise when his demonic heritage manifested. As his body twisted, Amaemon was forced to flee far from the surface. The passage of time has only left him more obsessed with what he has lost - consumed by poison both physical and spiritual.

Once a hero among the titans, Antaeus grew jealous of the titan queen. In single combat he challenged and slew her, and for this crime he was exiled and descended into the Hells. Finding the inhabitants of that place no match for his might, Antaeus tore from its substance a fourth Hell, Cocytus, a realm born of frozen spite.

Once a talented human weaver, Arachne was transformed into a monstrous half-spider by a jealous rival's curse. Driven out of her village, she found sanctuary for a time among the jorogumo before a bitter feud forced her to flee once more. Now she wanders other corners of the dungeon with a small retinue of loyal students in tow, seeking a new domain in which they can spin their peerless tapestries in peace.

Greatest and most cunning of the Lords of Hell, Asmodeus was born when the twin fires of greed and treachery first sparked to life within a mortal's heart. His hideous body is perpetually wreathed in flame.

Once a king infamous for waging bloodthirsty campaigns, Asterion was exiled to the depths of the dungeon for his crimes. Here he lurks in his tattered finery, dreaming of a new kingdom. In his lust for power, the minotaur king turned to the worship of Makhleb, and Makhleb has rewarded him with horrifying destructive might.
A powerful, belligerent efreet. (Is there any other kind?)

A weary draconian with foreign and watery scales. She has come to the Dungeon in hopes of resurrecting her mortal husband; a noble cause, for a being once known for quarrelling with saints and flooding unfortunate temples. If pressed to her limits, she will reveal her true form, the mere sight of which struck her husband dead. Adventurers may wish they were so lucky!

Once a gangly and bedraggled vampire with a strange obsession with colour, Blorkula was offered succour by a missionary of Beogh and became a portly and vigorous orc with a strange obsession with colour instead. He wields magic tinged with every hue of the rainbow, and has mastered the art of dividing his own form among its many colours to avoid killing blows - though even he must rest a while before doing so a second time.

An ancient and powerful lich. Like all true liches, Boris is immortal, and will regenerate his desiccated skeletal remains even if completely disintegrated. The same cannot be said for his many victims over his many centuries, from which he collects and channels their dying woes and regrets.

As a young woman, Cassandra bound herself in service to Ashenzari and was blessed and cursed in equal measure - granted the ability to foresee disasters, but only those she was powerless to prevent. Eventually driven from her homeland as a harbinger of the very plagues she'd spent a lifetime warning against, she has come to the dungeon in her final days in hope of averting one last catastrophe.
A violent and wrathful demon, Cerebov appears as a giant humanoid covered in shining golden armour and wielding a huge twisted sword.
Chuck the stone giant loves rocks, the bigger the better! Over the years, he has managed to amass quite the collection, including some rare, enchanted ones.
A withered old gnoll with a long silver beard, wielding a quarterstaff and wearing a cloak. He looks like a figure from mythology! Wait, is his beard held on to his ears with hooks?

Greatest and most ruthless of the Lords of Hell, Dispater was born when first an iron sword drank mortal blood. They despise mortal vanities, the pursuit of ‘reason’ and ‘beauty’ - the only art they enjoy is the art of war.

The Pits of Slime used to be a thriving civilisation, and Dissolution was the prophet of their god. When the city was overtaken by its current residents, only Dissolution survived, for they alone turned faithfully to the Slime God. Dissolution became a tremendous mass of acidic ooze, yet retained their intelligence. They are filled with hatred for anything that can hold a form.

{{ local descript = "An adventurer just like you, trying to find the Orb." if you.race() ~= "Merfolk" and you.race() ~= "Octopode" then descript = descript .. " Unlike you, and d" else descript = descript .. " D" end descript = descript .. "espite his hatred of it, he takes to water " .. "like a fowl." return descript }}

A beautiful but vain deep elf with an aptitude for magic and little else. His skills are the perfect complement of his twin sister Duvessa's fighting prowess. In search of more powerful spells, he journeys to the surface with his sister.

A plain-looking deep elven fighter who is technically brilliant in many forms of combat, but over-confident because of it. She is complemented by the magical skills of her twin brother, Dowan. She journeys to the surface to challenge its greatest champions.

A jealous sibling of Sigmund (indeed, the youngest of nine brothers). He has none of Sigmund's skills in magic, but makes up for it with his skills in fighting and a canny head for money. He is eager to prove his superiority by killing hapless adventurers with his expensive flail and quick wit.
First and most fearful of her kind, the Enchantress rules over the spriggans of the dungeon. She wears an opalescent outfit made of dragon skin that shimmers with many colours.

Greatest and most inexorable of the Lords of Hell, Ereshkigal was born when first a mortal breathed her last. Noiselessly she laughs at lives cut short and loved ones separated by untimely death, enwreathed in the silence of the grave.
A wild-tempered adventuress. She's quite prideful for an octopode, and brandishes their venomous capacity and camouflage talents with cruel force.
An apprentice summoner with a flowing moustache. He has funny ideas about honour.
A cold-hearted elven sorcerer, draped in robes of high office. They whisper grimly to themself as they stalk the dungeon, trailing ice crystals through the air behind them.

A stout warrior who once bested a powerful lord of Pandemonium in combat, gaining control over the demon's realm and thanes. The battle left her with a deep facial scar, one that she carries as a badge of honour rather than a symbol of shame.
A svelte fighter-mage with a gold-rimmed monocle, a keen sense of tradition, and the blood of the gods running through his veins. He's here looking for a worthy opponent, but he's yet to find one.

A voracious and surprisingly intelligent slug, devoted to eating everything and everyone he comes across, with a pointed hat perched rakishly atop his head. He acquired the hat the same way he acquired his intelligence and his knowledge of spells: by consuming their former owner, a powerful wizard.
A huge, three-headed, winged arch-demon, guardian of the four Hells. Legends say that his silver horn can summon terrible beasts to aid him in battle.
A shadowy figure clothed in profound darkness.

An intrepid goblin who has somehow managed to tame a ghost moth as his mount. While the elaborate snarl of ropes he is using to remain upright on it surely undermines the moth's own mobility, even a hobbled ghost moth can be a deadly adversary. And Goji? Well. He's also here.
An inefficient shadow imp previously employed as a torturer in one of the lower circles of Hell. She has a tendency to complain and make inane statements.
A tough-looking gnoll, wearing the pelt of one of his former war dogs.

A brutally twisted undead gnoll in the eternal service of Ereshkigal, lord of Tartarus. Legend has it that he sold his soul to return his most beloved hunting dog to life. Whether that hound is a member of his current pack, none can say.
A middle-aged bounty hunter, anxious to retire after one final job. He hopes to settle down somewhere and live a quiet life with his family, using the money from his final bounty: you.

While a mortal cannot turn into a demon aside from divine intervention, this is what happened to Ignacio after Makhleb saw his love for his job and smiled upon him. He is now slated to continue the joy of his life for all eternity. Although his new form includes a number of large razor-sharp blades growing from his demonic appendages, he kept his favourite axe and is eager to let you test its edge.
A small and shrewd goblin inventor, wearing blue rags coated in soot. She claims dominion over this level of the dungeon; trespassers will find themselves on the business end of a homemade wand.
A deadly merfolk water-witch, who uses her dominion over the tides to draw unwitting adventurers to their deaths.

Jeremiah was a peaceful dreamer, prone to impromptu naps. They slipped into slumber while gazing into a magical orb, and dreamed of an old and hateful power binding them into service. Now Jeremiah stumbles through the dungeon, searching for the precious dreamshard that will restore their master’s power, unsure whether they wake or slumber still. Their dreams leak into reality in the form of a constant stream of butterflies.
An evil apprentice sorceress. She entered the dungeon hoping to find a quiet, secluded place where she could study the darker arts without being disturbed.
A dwarven magician, particularly well-attuned to the dungeon around him. He wields powerful earth magic in combat.

Once a simple village peasant, Jory found himself transformed in undeath into a powerful creature. Through the countless centuries unlived since then, he has honed his skills in combat and magic, and amassed great wealth and many possessions.
Looks like a mercenary in a stupid-looking hat.

A fearsome necromancer who followed her craft beyond the limits of flesh and life. Her pursuit of demonic knowledge left her body ruined, but the powers she gained allowed her to rebuild her missing limbs from glittering ice.
A formidable necromancer, committed to her craft even after it left her aged, decaying, and half-undead herself.
An incredibly powerful emperor on the way to godhood. He died quite some time ago, but he sees no reason why that should stop him.
A master of transformation and treachery. Beware, or you may be the next swine to join her herd!

A huge beast, mightiest of hydras, infamous in myth and legend. It flows through the water faster than a human can run, swatting aside trees as though they were matchsticks. Its many heads slaver and gnash constantly as it hunts for prey to slake its bottomless appetite.

An ogre emissary of the Ironbound Order, sent to find and stop intruders before they enter the Vaults. Fiercely charismatic, he's rallied a small army of his kin, overawing them with the long-range lightning array he wears on his back. (The large coin purse he took from the Vaults is also quite persuasive.)

Stoic and inscrutable, Lom Lobon is an ancient demon infamous for their mastery of magic. Rumoured to be the most learned being in the halls of Pandemonium, they are at times sought out by mortal wizards who offer their souls in exchange for the secrets of the arcane. Lacking the terrible wrath present in most demons, Lom Lobon's single eye instead hides a cold, impartial cruelty.

A mighty sorceress, clad from head to toe in heavy armour. Once an adventurer looking for the fabled Orb of Zot, she was cast into the Abyss and got hopelessly lost there. Toyed with by some greater power, she was stuck on the hostile plane for nearly a decade. When she finally emerged from the Abyss, Louise had become powerful indeed, but had also gone fully insane. She now wanders the halls of the dungeon, seeking other adventurers to share her fate.

This tall and powerful demon is Mara, Lord of Illusions, mighty among dreamers. He is capable of creating intricately detailed illusions, so real that they are almost as deadly as the creatures they impersonate.

In a distant time, Maggie was apprenticed to the dreaded Hell Knights - but she grew impatient. In search of a shortcut to fame and fortune (and somewhat short on imagination), she entered the Dungeon and set out to slay a dragon. Now having slain one, Maggie sees no reason to stop.

A lithe spellcaster in service to the powers of Hell; it is her duty to ensure that the inhabitants of the Dungeon never forget their place. She personally slew the ancient dragon from whose hide her strange armour is crafted.

A sly, conniving thief. A self-proclaimed legend, he was one of the most skilled and crafty of the thieves and rogues lured by the Orb. The magical parasitic vines that have claimed his body still wish to continue his life's work, with a back-up plan of both a vicious magic-drinking maw and potent wands.

A fair and noble ruler of an ancient and mighty kingdom, mummified after an early death. His faithful priests subsequently infused him with great and powerful magic, seeking to grant him eternal life. Now he is forgotten and reduced to mouldering bandages and dry, brittle bones.

There was once a human priest named Mennas. He travelled far and wide as a missionary of Zin, often venturing even into Orcish lands. He beseeched the orcs to abandon their false tribes and return to the peoples of their birth; only Zin's light could truly cleanse the weight of sin that had twisted their bodies. By all accounts the orcs were not happy with Mennas. Eventually, a group of them demanded he recant his words and when Mennas remained silent, they cut out his tongue. Whether or not this angel is that same Mennas is something of a mystery, as he seems to have difficulty speaking.

A demon prince once possessed a hunger for power that was exceptional even by the standards of his kind. He betrayed his realm to Lugonu, and his reward was to become this twisted mass of corruption, now known only as Mlioglotl.
A weirdly glowing figure, dancing through the twisted air of Pandemonium.
A demonic skull rolling along the ground.

A fast-moving magical cat. Once a powerful wizard's familiar, Natasha was abandoned after her master was consumed by the very necromantic forces he sought to control. Now she patrols the dungeon, taking a bloody vengeance with spell and claw upon any adventurer who crosses her path. This cat doesn't have nine lives, but just one death isn't going to be enough to put her down for good.
A highly intelligent elephant who travelled as part of a circus. One dark night, she slipped out of her chain and disappeared into Pandemonium, never to be seen again.

A shrewd and wizened orc who has devoted her life to chronicling the bloody history of her people. She claims to know the names and deeds of every last orc who lost their life in their great exodus into the Dungeon, and even if this is a lie, she nonetheless seems to be on a first-name basis with many of them. More than any other orc still breathing, she knows the blood and sacrifice it took to make this place a refuge for her kind. She will not brook its being intruded upon by anyone - least of all you.
A centaur warrior, skilled at warfare and deceit. They slew a mighty hydra, and now its deadly blood drips, still-fuming, from their arrows.
A brilliant scientist obsessed with electricity. In his attempts to perfect his electric golem, he was involved in a terrible accident, and now phases in and out of reality.

A time-lost revenant, risen not from the death of a single individual but of many - its bones fused together from the young and the elderly and different species altogether. Whether they were all the victims of a single massacre or a thousand souls discarded over a thousand years is impossible to say now; history does not remember them. But one thing is clear: they will fight to change that until every last memory they have left burns away.
A relaxed water cultist with a healthy tan and a soothing voice. He doesn't really care if it is you or he who dies — “both” would probably be the best option.

An unusually strong troll, his thick frame scarred by many against-the-odds victories. He has been wounded so many times that his body has adapted, and now heals almost instantly. His necklace of troll claws is a memento of those who underestimated him.

A wise kobold would fear the forces of Hell, and certainly would not set up a highly lucrative transdimensional trade in damned souls. But Pikel is better known for his whip than his wisdom, mercilessly tormenting his piteous charges as he ferries them to their buyers.

A cyclops shepherd, he is very protective of his charges, whom he watches with an undying fervor through his single massive eye. Nevertheless, he won't hesitate to use them as projectiles in a pinch; after all, the best defence is a good offence.
A frog of unusual size, with a tiny crown perched incongruously atop his head.

A mountain hobgoblin, recently come in search of the legendary Orb. Not foolhardy or reckless enough to delve into the depths of the Dungeon alone, Robin has built a small army of minions. Potential competitors will quickly find a stream of screaming goblins flying toward them!
A strikingly realistic sapphire statue of a famous earth mage who disappeared after a catastrophic mishap with a magical talisman.

Rippling muscles, glistening pecs, incredible glutes - Rupert is the peak of physical perfection. Even so, his roars seem louder than even his fantastic form can explain. Perhaps he holds some talisman that lends supernatural force to his bellows?
A mighty warlord. Some orcs even say they are the Chosen One of Beogh.

The elder of a pair of brothers who came for the Orb. No one knows what Sigmund saw in the dungeon to drive him mad, but his shrewd magical tactics and wicked scythe now leave little time for his victims to wonder. Despite his reputation as a vicious murderer, his grandiose and dramatic ways have earned him the admiration of many denizens of the dungeon.
A particularly corpulent troll with a short temper and a sizable gut. Uninterested in the Orb, Snorg delights in the endless parade of adventurers – that is, easy meals — it attracts.

A former beekeeper's apprentice with an ambitious dream: to modernise the whole world's beekeeping industry with the smooth certainty of disease-proof metal. His methods may be questionable and his goals dubious, but his prototype's stinger still looks awfully sharp...
Queen of the tengu, with legendary skill in swordsmanship, tactics, and magic. Storytellers claim she once trapped a raging tempest in a bottle and kept it as a talisman.
A graceful kobold assassin. Admire her graceful pirouettes, thrill at her daring leaps! But watch out for her knives!
A veteran of a war against the armataurs' elephant-riders. He has recently retired to make a new home in the dungeon.
The earthly avatar of Tiamat, deity of dragonkind, here incarnated as a mighty draconian warrior. Her scales seem to shimmer and change colour as you watch.

A coarse and lanky orc. Urug lost her eye in a fight with a harpy, and has sworn to slay every last one of them. Unfortunately, the vision in her remaining eye is not very good, and she has mistaken you for one. {{ if you.can_smell() then return "She smells terrible." end }}
A cantankerous dwarf wearing a stupid-looking hat. He eyes you sourly, as if deciding exactly how much offence he should take to the way you're staring at it.
An elite marksnaga who leads a skilled team of sharpshooters. She is particularly skilled in translocation magic.

One of the Stoneborn, formed untold aeons ago with supreme command over rock. Her people shelter deep within the living earth, so whatever has forced Vv into the oppressive openness of the Dungeon must be dire indeed. But whatever it is, she's not talking...

It has been centuries since outsiders were last allowed access to the cavernous libraries of the formicids, but their emissaries are still seen from time to time - surveying other lands for resources or scientific discoveries that might aid the colony. This one's study of the magical fibres excreted by orb spiders has already led to an alchemical breakthrough, allowing them to shape fulminant prisms such that their explosions are directed at enemies alone. Alas, their enthusiasm to conduct a field test bodes poorly for your health.

A master weaponsmith, her flesh melding into steel so smoothly that it's hard to tell where one ends and the other begins. She entered the Dungeon to search for the secrets of an ancient, long-suppressed cult, said to have exalted metal over flesh. The price of knowledge was her humanity - a price she paid eagerly.
A huge, red-glowing, three-headed dragon, shrouded in damnation. It is possessed by the very essence of Gehenna and its eternal fire.
A massive white three-headed dragon, covered with shards of gleaming ice, wholly possessed by the nightmarish cold of Cocytus.
A towering three-headed beast with an army's worth of swords for teeth. Each of its scales is a shield with a razored edge.
Seemingly three pairs of lurid magenta eyes hanging in the darkness, the outline of a vast, sinuous dragon is just barely perceptible behind. Its malice is palpable.

A missionary in the service of Lugonu, with remnants of its headless body spilling from a roaming spatial rift. It seeks to teach others the joy and strength of slowly decoupling from this particular plane of reality.
A lump of sickly pustulent flesh, dripping with lethal acid.
A small dragon with brilliant yellow scales, its mouth dripping with corrosive slime.
A common dungeon snake, a species of troglodytic reptile commonly found in subterranean spaces.
A spirit drawn from the elemental plane of air. It exists in this world as a lightning-spitting spirit, stunning foes with its crackling bursts.
A floating shard of crystaline jade which resonates with your air magic.
A self-styled monarch of a shambling black alder, half respected and half ridiculed by other fae. It backs up its aspirations to sovereignty with unearthly vile magic quite close to a touch of death.
An aggressive crocodilian with great crunching jaws full of sharp teeth.
A particularly large and nasty snapping turtle. Like its smaller relative, it can reach out and bite from afar.
A very large snake that moves with startling swiftness. It kills not by poison but by constricting its prey.

A humanoid construct of insubstantial memory, floating through the air. Though perhaps somewhat changed in shape and bearing few discernable features, still they seem somehow to resemble a warrior from the distantly remembered past. The memory and the memorialist fight in concert, each able to fire past the other.
An unfathomably ancient skeleton. It has hundreds of golden sigils etched onto its bones, and pulses with terrible, unholy power.
A lich who, having existed for countless centuries, has grown almost unimaginably powerful through the study of dark magic.
