A nexus of sentient cancer and disease, borne aloft perhaps by malice alone. Its nature inflicts withering illness on all living beings in its presence.
A divine warrior of the Shining One. It is a towering winged figure of unnatural beauty surrounded by an aura of brilliant white light.
A placid, sacred bull of Elyvilon. Its status as an exalted envoy of the Healer lets its very presence double the health of its allies.
An opalescent crab with jet black eyes, and chaotic mists effusing from its mandibles. Rumours claim that this species is waiting for the end of time.
A wizard fond of spectacle and destruction. They scorn the cowardice of other magicians, who hide from their foes rather than simply blasting them out of existence.

The sweat and toil of the armourer working leather and steel infuses an intention into their creation, a unique spark within every cuirass, pauldron and vambrace. A skilled forgewright can manifest these intentions in physical form, allowing their armour to protect its wearer in a more aggressive fashion than armour customarily does.

The divided and churning remains of a protean progenitor, striving desperately for form. Whatever they become, the last of their progenitor's power ensure it will be stronger and swifter than any such creature found elsewhere in the dungeon.
An oversized insect with dagger-sharp forcipules and a great abundance of limbs. Its sting injects crippling toxins whose potency increases as they mature.
An extremely cold blob of bright blue cytoplasm, forming bits of frost in the air around it.
A swift sphere of coruscating electrical energy. It will explode at the slightest disturbance.
A small snake that can augment its bite by constricting small creatures.

A lumpy reddish fungus covered in knobbly rhizome growths, growing well in the dank underground dungeon. When it senses a threat, the ballistomycete may release a deadly floating spore that explodes on its victims.

A fast, gas-filled floating spore released by a ballistomycete when it senses a threat. After seeking out its foe, the spore will explode, damaging anything caught in the blast and further confusing living creatures.
A huge and very powerful demon, wreathed in fire and shadows.
An amphibious humanoid with a very ugly attitude.
A crested lizard of middling size with a terrible petrifying gaze.
A large grey bat that, despite being herbivorous, is quite aggressive. It is myopic and uses echolocation to navigate.

A scintillating and ever-changing prism of pure chaos that resonates with its partner's actions. Each time its partner performs a melee attack, it will launch a barrage of chaotic energy at a random enemy and change its form. After doing this several times, it will become fully charged and stop resonating with attacks. If its partner casts a spell in this state, it will violently release its stored power with an effect that scales to the level of spell used: Level 1-4: Blast 3 random enemies with chaos.\n Level 5-7: Blast 5 random enemies with chaos and create shooting stars.\n Level 8-9: Blast 7 random enemies with chaos explosions and create even more shooting stars.
A small globe of destructive energy. Each time its creator casts an offensive spell, it will launch a magical barrage at the most injured nearby foe it can reach.
A sacred, self-created sunbird, representative of rebirth. It has ascended past the cycles of life and death, and calls upon aspects of both, rising forth from death in a burst of unholy flame.
A minor hairy maggot spirit, phasing in and out of this plane. Each regional variant inflicts different minor ailments: the ones found in the Dungeon cause one's magic to grow weak.
A small black bear. Like all ursines, it will become enraged if badly hurt.
A muscular black-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and powerful wings.
An astonishingly fast tropical snake whose bite bears a deadly venom.
The exposed elemental core of a blazeheart golem. Far too unstable to remain without its shell, it is in the process of violently exploding.
A volatile elemental spark encased in a shell of slag iron. If destroyed while its fires still blaze, the exposed core will violently detonate a moment later.
A species of frog that possesses the ability to blink at will. It can blink itself close to its intended prey, or blink away to escape harm. It is commonly found in packs.
A greater demon formed from wistful snow and bitter lightning.
A decaying undead corpse. When it reaches a victim (or if it's destroyed first), the gases trapped inside it are released and create a large, violent concussive blast.
A block of ice shaped like a statue, but worked by no living hands.
An undead figure preserved by the brackish waters of a bog, and reanimated by some unknown magic.
A malevolent and dangerous little sprite. The shadowy illusions it summons may not be real, but are deadly all the same.

An unassuming beetle filled with an incredible amount of hypergolic fluid. The sticky spray it fires is capable of igniting predators and unwary adventurers alike, though more experienced ones know to keep moving if they wish to avoid a fiery grave.
A small metal sphere surrounding a core of dormant fire magic. When given the proper command, it will detonate in a blast of metal and flame that is only partially affected by fire resistance.

A mighty undead abomination, pieced together from the broken bones of many dragons by powerful necromantic magic. The collective despair of such desecrated dragons gives this horror its own undying breath weapon, in billowing clouds of excruciating misery.
A mass of fast-rolling stone, crushing everything in its path.

A grey beetle with an almost impenetrable rocky carapace. When at some distance from its foe, a boulder beetle is capable of rolling at high speed, attempting to crash into its target for heavy damage.
The soul of a living, holy, or demonic creature, captured by a dark sacrifice to Yredelemnul. The bound soul will follow its captor through stairs and come when recalled from a different level.

An impossible shape that scintillates with unearthly colour. The power of Zot flows heavily through it, overlaying this reality with countless others where its domain remains pristine. Each tesseract is inextricably linked to the other, and destroying one will destroy both (and expel all the creatures they have beckoned to this reality, as well as dazing even those which they have not). But so long as they are allowed to exist, there will be no end to the forces which seek to keep you from the Orb.
A slimy fluorescent worm with a greatly distended head. This creature feeds on others' intellect as it squirms through unworldly grime.

A tangled cluster of thorny briars, sharp enough to pierce thick hide and armour. Although stationary, its branches are possessed with a will of their own. They move to allow magic and missiles fired by those friendly to this plant to pass through unaffected.
A huge and powerful demon wreathed in damnation, with great scaly wings. It is one of the most fearsome denizens of any of the Hells.
A giant spider swollen with eggs. Its innumerable offspring are always at its call.
A masked priest in the service of Kikubaaqudgha, well-versed in choral rituals to both rouse the dead and send them to eternal rest.
A rapidly-growing mushroom whose life-cycle culminates in an explosive release of spores. These spores have a mild psychoactive effect and can sometimes daze creatures who breathe them in.

A woody plant. It looks dry enough to be easily set on fire, and its foliage is not very dense, permitting both magic and missiles to pass through unaffected. However, it is firmly rooted, and requires significant effort to destroy.

An unusually aggressive amphibian that pursues its prey with rapid hops. Its croak is loud and distinctive, but unlike its smaller counterparts above ground, the dungeon bullfrog is as large as it sounds.
A flesh-eating beast that uses its limbs and tail interchangeably. It moves with alarming speed, but must pause to reorganise itself after each attack. Its distinctive screams carry far and wide.
A large, brightly coloured butterfly with beautifully patterned wings, fluttering incongruously through the darkness of the cave.
A green-skinned, spiny colossus, with a hearty barrel chest and a thirst for battle. Any foe that strikes it in melee will be lucky to live to regret it.
A maniacal demon, brimming with accursed power. Its gleeful laughter rarely ceases, even in the heat of battle.
A hideous toad whose thick, warty hide is covered in poison glands. Unlike its smaller above-ground relatives, this dungeon-dweller is the size of a wolf.
A sluggish black buffalo, its hide encrusted with dull scales. It carries its hog-like head just above the ground, protected by a stiff mane of bristles. Its fearsome breath turns flesh into stone.
A swift, nightmarish bird whose razor-sharp metallic feathers drip with corrosive acid.

A balloon-like sac of slime mold spores, suspended in a nutrient slurry to sustain them on their search for a new home. To the great misfortune of any adventurers in the vicinity, this slurry is also a highly potent acid.
A hybrid with the torso of a human atop the body of a horse. It is highly skilled in archery.
A muscular centaur, veteran of numerous battles, armed with well-made weapons and able to use them skilfully.
A small, wilful minor demon. Its wings, far larger than its scrawny body, were made to soar, and it lands only rarely and with the greatest reluctance.
A being of pure chaos, its form is constantly shifting, growing and then losing eyes, mouths, claws and tentacles. It corrupts everything it touches.

A throne-bearer of the gods, whose head is beset by four faces: one of a man, one of an ox, one of a lion, one of an eagle. It is one of the angelic beings who stand before the good gods, singing eternal hymns of praise to their glory and greatness.

Some sorcerers care little for unholy realms or undead forms, seeking power instead in the whims of cruel chaos. This ominous owl-winged head is all that remains of a former archmage: it delights in spreading misfortune and drinking blood in its new airborne form.

A common dungeon pest that combines the worst features of a scavenging insect and a looming deadline. Time flows strangely around it, rewinding any injuries inflicted upon it unless the source of them is near enough to be caught up in its timestream.

A wizened, headless corpse, animated not by conventional necromancy but by the mournful malice of dead stars. Its psychic eyes, floating disjointedly from its body's movements, relentlessly burrow through its victims' minds.

A mechanical insect powered by an intricate array of gears and springs. It is vicious and resilient to damage, but its clockwork naturally winds down as it attacks, eventually leaving it unable to move until its creator winds it again.
An unfathomably massive pile of mystic pulsating protoplasm. The slightest threat will cause it to undergo rapid weaponised mitosis, rapidly overwhelming potential meals in a cytoplasmic tidal wave.

A modern breakthrough in arcane experimentation, this mobile prison cell weaponises the living fragments of once-escaped ugly things, extending the reach of their tendrils to thrash multiple foes at once from a distance.
A formless mass of ancient fire, bound by heat and malevolence. It longs to unleash itself as a wild fire storm, yet must first patiently burn towards its victims with implaceable inevitability.
An enormous and unnervingly motile slime mold colony. It creeps along the crevices of the walls in search of nutrients and can spread itself to new locations by launching enormous sporangia.
A small, ugly minor demon. Its fanged maw seems locked in a permanent malign grin, and its horns protrude obscenely from its scaly pate.
A spiny, long snouted rodent grown out of pure living crystal. It is immune to most forms of magic and hurls both crystallising shots and painful barbs.

An intricate animated statue made of heavily ensorcelled crystal that is immune to most forms of magic. The spells which created it are so powerful that even flesh may start to crystallise around any fragments that become embedded in it - leaving its foes brittle and vulnerable.
A small spider with rudimentary healing abilities. Though not undead, it packs a nasty vampiric bite.
A charred skull floating in the air and rotating slowly. Mystic symbols are carved into its blackened surface.
A disembodied toe, hanging in the air and radiating an intense field of negative energy.
A giant with one eye in the centre of its forehead. Despite its lack of binocular vision, it is able to throw boulders with fearsome accuracy.
A towering winged figure radiating an aura of brilliant golden light. It is a divine agent of the Shining One.
A weapon enchanted to dance through the air and attack under its own power.
A small invertebrate. It hunts prey considerably larger than itself by firing chitinous darts, using a concealed air bladder to launch them with remarkable range and power.
A noxious and deadly fungus suffused with negative energy. While parasitic in life, undeath has granted it the ability to absorb its nutrients directly from the life force of others.
A dreadful undead cob of maize. Look, this one was probably a mistake. We're sorry.
A dark and baleful minor dragon. It breathes a lethally potent miasma from its pestilential maw.
A warrior-priest of Yredelemnul, chanting fearful supplications to its dark god.
A hideous swarming undead insect, exuding death and decay and feeding on the life energies of those unfortunate enough to encounter it.
A larger and beefier relative of the common dungeon yak. Its little red eyes gleam with hunger for living flesh.
A deep elf who exults in conjured mayhem and destruction. It is widely hated and feared, both for the power and for the precision of its destructive magics.
An experienced deep elf fighter with a penchant for ranged combat.
A champion of the deep elves, who scorns magic and is devoted to the study of the sword. It wields two weapons with astonishing dexterity and speed.
A deep elf surrounded by a shimmering aura of negative energy, as a result of its practice of necromancy and life-sapping magic.
A deep elf who is marked heavily by long years of contact with unnatural demonic forces and the creatures of the Abyss.
A deep elf commanding the primal forces of the universe. It is renowned for its ability to pin down even the most elusive foes with powerful, unavoidable magic.
An exalted servant of the ancient dark god of the deep elves, basking in hellish death magic.
A deep elf archer who has devoted a lifetime to the mastery of archery, dismissing magic as a frivolous distraction.
A deep elf learned in the ways of fiery magic. It is capable of casting a wide array of scorching spells.
A mighty spellcaster who draws power from the very Hells, and possesses lethal arcane abilities.
An elf with a singular focus on the magic of the air, leaving little time to study anything else.
A stooped troll with dark skin. It often travels in packs.
A particularly intelligent deep troll. It uses its magic to tunnel through the earth and ambush foes.
A deep troll blessed with divine power to strengthen and hasten its kin.
A human-like figure with an aura of power betraying its divine ancestry.
A hellish insectoid creature, fueled by some infernal power that constantly regrows its chitinous segments. Nothing short of a lethal blow will stop it for long.
A half-mortal, half-demonic creature, with its hellish heritage asserting itself through a certain devilish cast to its features.
A half-mortal, half-demonic creature, radiating an intense heat. It weaves powerful and unpredictable spells of devastation.
A half-mortal, half-demonic creature, oozing with dark energies. It twists space around itself, and can corrupt weapons, armour and even the very flesh of its opponents.
A half-mortal, half-demonic creature, covered in icy blue scales. Its devotion to the deities of death grants it great insight into the vulnerabilities and applications of mortal souls.

A half-mortal, half-demonic creature, now more beast than whatever species it is descended from. It is devoted to martial combat, disrupting the magic of its foes as it feasts off of endless conflict.
A serrated disc forged of razor-sharp material. It spins in place at high velocity, shredding through flesh and metal alike.
A towering obelisk surrounded by a powerful storm.
A huge pachyderm, wilder and fiercer than normal elephants, with a very thick hide, powerful legs, and a memory to die for.
An elemental spirit formed from smokeless fire.

A demon lapdog of the queen of Tartarus, bound to hunt her enemies. The first time a foe hears its howl, it will echo in their mind, calling nightmarish creatures to hunt them. Those who survive have the small consolation of being inoculated against that particular hound's howl.
A mechanical insect powered by an intricate array of gears and springs. It has run out of power and can only be rewound by its creator moving into it.
A brown-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and small wings. It is yet to develop the distinct colouring and powerful breath attack of its mature form.
A draconian that uses powerful conjurations to destroy anyone who dares to stand in its way.
A draconian protected by thick scales, skilful weapon use, and complementary magic.
A draconian who has eschewed the study of weaponry and magic in order to train in the art of unarmed combat. Its scaly fists, well-thewed legs, and mighty tail rain down blows upon its opponents.
A cunning draconian who has mastered the inner secrets of the element of fire. Its scales are sooty from years of magical pyrotechnics.
A draconian master of the warp, who can translocate both itself and anyone else to any place, either on this world or outside of it.
A draconian deriving its thunderous powers and draconic allies from the worship of Qazlal.
A territorial gnarl of driftwood and shattered bones. Its resentment of the living has slowly twisted its remains into a monstrous form, capable of brandishing weapons and spreading terrible curses.
A lich who has made terrible pacts with demonic forces to augment its dark magic.
A drowsy, fluffy ovine whose coat sparkles with motes of dream dust. It gathers in herds and fills the air with dream dust, overwhelming its victims and putting them to sleep.

A cold and hollow apparition of the drowned dead, chained by some lingering attachment to the depths in which it perished. It rushes to embrace the living, sharing the last moments of its watery fate with whatever it touches.
A conniving demon born from the nightmares of sleeping mages. It delights in coaxing the imagined fears of mortals into reality.
A spirit of nature, bound to the forest in which it resides. It is capable of calling upon the trees to defend against incursions.
A member of a short, sturdy mountain-dwelling folk.
A spirit drawn from the elemental plane of earth. It exists in this world as a sinuous stream of silt and stone, capable of smoothly flowing through solid rock.
A floating shard of crystaline jade which resonates with your earth magic.
An imposing, muscular figure engulfed in a cloud of searing flame.
An ancient skeletal apparition, sheathed in a cloud of mist. Its form glows white-hot with debilitating energy.
An immense, squamous appendage of some unseen creature, dripping with ichor and tipped with a single, terrible-looking claw.
A part of an immense, squamous appendage. It thrashes and pulsates like no other living thing.
An animated figure made completely of electricity, created in some demented wizard's experiment.
A type of fish capable of generating a powerful electric field.

Spirits of marshes and bogs. From the cypresses and willows of the fens stems the power of these fierce protective spirits. With the boughs and branches they flow, emerging from trees near their foes to strike.
A swirling conflux of elemental water streaming from the elemental plane into this one, with powerful spirits and mighty floods flowing from it.

A humanoid construct of insubstantial memory, floating through the air. Though perhaps somewhat changed in shape and bearing few discernable features, still it seems somehow to resemble a mage from the distantly remembered past, skilled with destructive elemental magic.
A large, thick-hided pachyderm. It crushes its foes and then thrashes them with its trunk.
A giant scorpion with a massive barb on its tail dripping deadly venom. It is one of the largest arachnids known.

A glob of grey sludge that has somehow developed a rudimentary awareness and limited motility. It periodically draws heat from its surroundings to sustain itself, freezing enemies unfortunate enough to be adjacent at the time.
A gaunt humanoid with flaking, pale chitin. Its spindly limbs are capable of startlingly quick movement and end in razor-sharp talons.

A churning mass of flowing blood that throbs to the beat of an absent heart. Does it wish to bury itself in your arteries because it recognises, on some primordial level, that this is where it belongs? Alas, all it is capable of in this fleeing moment of sentience is violence.
A two-headed giant, stronger than most, and able to land devastating blows left and right with its two huge weapons.
A horribly powerful and swift demon, its shape obscured by a cloud of swirling scythe-like blades.
A huge eyeball, encased in a levitating globe of incandescent energy.
A hovering horror, rare and unnatural even amongst servitor eyes, radiating baleful energies. They monitor the flow of chaotic life and ever-present death for the divine Jiyva.
A hybrid with the torso of a human atop the forelegs of a goat. It is fabled for its ability to play with the minds of those who intrude into its domain.
A feline creature that has been granted sentience by magical means. It uses the gift of speech to demand milk, treats and catnip.
Followers of the ancient swamp ways, these witches rise above the muck and mire on a pair of stilt-like chicken legs. They are masters of pain and poison.
A floating shard of crystaline jade which resonates with your fire magic.
A bat whose leathery body burns with a hot flame.

A variety of crab prized for its brilliantly jewelled shell. The rarity of the shells is only enhanced by its almost supernatural ability to wade through molten lava and expel massive quantities of flames.
A great reptilian beast with powerful claws on its limbs, covered in thick red scales and with two huge bat-like wings. Little trails of smoke spill from its toothy maw.
A spirit drawn from the elemental plane of fire, which exists in this world as a brilliant column of raging flames.
A giant with obsidian skin and a wild mane of glowing red hair, holding aloft a fiery sword. Fire giants believe that they are destined to unite and burn the entire world to cinders.
A swirling cloud of flame. After striking a foe, it disintegrates.

A hideous floating undead creature, the anguished spirit of a tortured victim, with torn skin hanging from an emaciated body. It restlessly stalks the dungeon, inflicting the anguish it felt in life upon those still living.

A beneficent remnant of the countless mortal knights who serve the Shining One. Their hosts' role in the divine hierarchy is to guide and direct their legions in righteous moral warfare, though they may also call upon those mortals to defend themselves.
A lizard with a giant and colourful fringe folded around its neck. It flares its impressive frill at its victims while hissing angrily.
A sentient ant that walks upright and is competent at digging.
A gelatinous assemblage of tentacles and venom, leaving a glistening trail as it slides along. Surely such a mockery of life could not be natural..?
A thin wisp of flaming swamp gas. It will burn the first hostile thing it touches and then dissipate.
An incorporeal skeletal form surrounded by a cloud of freezing air, likely the remains of some unfortunate adventurer. It now floats slowly through the dungeon, seeking to share its fate with others.
A giant with blue skin and hair like ice and snow. Its eyes are as bleak as winter skies. It marches grimly into battle with a great, frosty axe and howling blasts of cold.
A slender prism of unstable, soft gold that crackles with barely-contained destructive energy. Any blow which cracks its fragile surface is likely to result in a violent explosion.

Through considerable effort, certain strains of fungi may be cultivated and mutated to ravenously parasitise living tissue. This particular variety has consumed the flesh and possessions of whatever intruder was fed to it and now serves as a roving guard, wielding scavenged armaments and its own explosive spores.
A lumpy {{ if you.branch() == "Gulch" then return "mauve"; else return "grey"; end }} fungus, growing well in the dank underground dungeon.
A granite statue of a hideous winged monster, somehow brought to life.
A crab twisted by proximity to negative energy. Apparitions of the dead swirl around it, only barely visible.
A vile interdimensional predator that feeds on the life force of living beings. It resembles an enormous, spiny moth.
A decayed cadaver, reanimated and accursed with a terrible hunger. It desires nothing but to feed on the flesh of the living, and will fell its victims with its vicious claws.
A floating eyeball formed from living glass. Only the divine Jiyva could form such a curious servitor.

A huge pulsating brain, floating just off the floor and glowing with mutagenic energies. It radiates a constant psychic influence upon nearby allies, using its vast intellect to empower their spellcasting abilities.
A shapeshifter which has lost control over its transformations, and is constantly changing form.
A taller and better-equipped relative of goblins, and ally of orcs. It is somewhat doglike in appearance.
A gnoll witch possessed by a spirit of spite which flashes out from behind their eyes. Its strange chants and ululations send other gnolls into a wild frenzy.
A commander of a pack of gnolls. Scars on its stout body give evidence of how it earned its rank.

A roiling sphere of intense destructive energies, drawn from the fabric of the Hells themselves. It pursues a designated target inexorably, growing in size as it travels. If it collides with either a creature or wall, it will explode violently - though its creator is protected from the wild destruction unleashed as it does so.

A shuddering, shimmering apparition borne from the drowned dead, repeatedly called to this plane by some cruel mystic experiment. It will share its memories and experiences of drowning in tainted waters with whatever it first touches, then dissipate.

A short, impatient and unfriendly humanoid. Goblins first appeared only a few years ago, but are now remarkably numerous. Sadly, no number of raucous goblin parties will put them in a welcoming mood toward adventurers.

Goblin clans fractured over the advent of steel exoskeletons long ago, prompting an experimental arms race for goblin hegemony. Some volunteered to join forces with other species, an alliance that has enabled capturing and taming wyverns. From uptop their majestic dragon-like mounts, these goblins swiftly soar about and skewer those who intrude upon their allies' domain.
A great winged dragon covered in shining golden scales. Legends say that its blood runs both hot and cold, and is venomous to boot.
A tiny and shimmering floating eye, swift as the wind and glistening like gold. It has a peculiarly hypnotic look.
A frog of exceptional size, for a frog. It lashes its prey with its tongue from a distance to coat them in its acidic stomach juices.
A levitating ball, covered in malignant eyes and humming with eldritch energies. Many is the adventurer ripped limb from limb by its dreadful eyeteeth.
A bloated form covered in oozing sores and exhaling clouds of lethal poison.
A muscular green-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and small wings.
A muscular grey-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and small wings.
An ancient warrior, embalmed and cursed to walk in undeath for eternity.

A rare and distinct member of scaly society, light and swift like a snake, yet also intelligent like a naga. It is said that a guardian serpent would rather die in battle than leave anything to an intruder.
A fearsome aged hybrid with a woman's head, a lion's body, and the wings of an eagle. It solemnly guards the temples and treasures of the Dungeon with a multitude of mind-clouding maledictions.

An ancient undead sorcerer, exhumed by the living divines Sheza and Sargol and forced to labour night and day to anchor them to the world. Even after the fall of the divine twins, it works to resurrect its fallen masters.
A bird-like creature with a human face that roams the coasts endlessly, feared for its sharp claws and harrying strikes.
An ordinary piece of armour, held in your haunting grip. It can attack nearby enemies, but must return to your side if you ever stray too far from it.
A ravenous brute of a demon - as much animal as person. Born from the residue of mortal depravity, it gorges itself on malice and magic alike.
An extremely large and aggressive swine, bred in Hell, whose breath burns its foes to ash.
A huge black dog with glowing red eyes, and smoke pouring from its fanged mouth.
A heavily armoured warrior, in league with the powers of Hell, and usually accompanied by other unsavoury beings of its ilk.
A unusually large rat. Its weird, knobbly orange skin glows with the infernal energies that spawned it.
A towering monolith constructed and possessed by demonic forces. A thousand eyes leer through slits in its jagged, spiked armour.
An abhorrent pachyderm, descendant of demons, burning from within with the fires of Hell.
A terrifying weapon hewn from molten rock. It rains fiery destruction down upon its creators' enemies.
A hateful demon, desirous to see all life destroyed by its damnation.
A hideous skeletal demon. It swoops through the air on powerful wings of ancient withered skin, taking sadistic joy from harrying those who would try to flee its grasp.

A mutated devotee of Lugonu, warped by years of living in the Abyss. It has ascended into an exalted representative of Lugonu's spite against the rest of all existence and solemnly tears apart reality in Lugonu's name.

A humanoid construct of insubstantial memory, floating through the air. Though perhaps somewhat changed in shape and bearing few discernable features, still it seems somehow to resemble a warrior from the distantly remembered past, ready with debilitating spells and deadly knifework.

A large creature with the hindquarters of a horse and the wings, head and talons of a great eagle. As popular heraldric creatures, some fortresses may keep them as symbols and defenders alike, where they in turn launch intruders into the waiting blades of their masters.
An elegant siege weapon, magically sculpted from crystalline ice. As ephemeral as a summer snowstorm, every salvo it fires consumes a portion of itself until nothing is left behind but water.
A larger and even ruder goblin. Hobgoblins are perfectly capable of wielding weapons, but most prefer to beat their opponents to death with their bare hands.
A large even-toed ungulate. Like human beings, it is omnivorous, intelligent, and nearly hairless.
A rare celestial version of a usually filthy animal, said to be an angelic being who succumbed to hostile magic.
An aggressively territorial primate, known for the astonishing variety and volume of noise it can produce.
An uppity sort of surface-dwelling, hairless ape. Dwarves think of them as fragile, elves think of them as clumsy, and monsters think of them as tasty.

A great and nightmarish lacertilian beast. It has many heads, and the potential to grow many more! Hitting it with any bladed weapon bigger than a short blade risks lopping a head off and causing two more to grow in its place. Very large claws, such as trolls', are long enough to do the same. Only a weapon branded with flame will cauterise the wound and prevent more heads from growing.
The shed tail of a hypnogecko, still pulsing with mesmerising colours and compelling any nearby predators to focus their attention on it instead of the unfortunate lizard it once belonged to.
A terrible creature, formed of snow and crystalline ice. Its feet leave puddles of icy water on the floor.
A man-sized demon covered in glittering ice.
A white, frost-coated dragon. Snowflakes trickle from its nostrils.
A huge frigid demon covered in frost and wreathed in freezing air. It is one of the most terrible denizens of the many Hells.
An imposing idol of some nameless arctic god, carved in glistening deep blue ice. Freezing vapours swirl about it, and a chill pervades the air.
A floating shard of crystaline jade which resonates with your ice magic.
A green lizard with strong jaws and sharp teeth, prized for its flesh.
A warrior initiated in the mysteries of a dying cult, dedicated to serve thrones long-fallen. Its blows strip away magical defences, leaving its foes vulnerable to even the simplest hexes.

A mystical canine, frequently bound into the service of wizards and sorcerers. Its eyes flicker with remarkable intelligence, but its bite is no less sharp than its wilder cousins. They are difficult to truly kill - when gravely wounded, they instead return to spiritual form to lick their wounds until ready to be summoned again.
A very heavy, slow and apparently flightless dragon. It is named for its scales, which are so tough they might be iron. Small flakes of metal trail from its nostrils.
A rare and powerful spirit from the elemental plane of earth, it exists in this world by inhabiting a hulking mass of iron.
A huge, rusting monolith, larger than any other species of giant. It packs an incredible punch.
A large, ponderous and very solid statue of metal, given the power of locomotion through some esoteric means.
An ugly, twisted little minor demon with metal skin.
A great troll, mighty of limb and plated with thick scales that resemble lightly rusted iron, especially in their hardness.
A cruel and unruly brute who growls in the language of the untamed. Its very presence provokes and overworks non-sapient, living beasts and slimes alike into a rapid fervour.
A guardian mage clad in pattern-etched armour. It can recite words of power to summon distant allies and imbue them with unnatural might.
An emaciated warrior-mage, bound to guard long-coveted treasures. It calls forth deadly frost from its surrounds, freezing foes that are next to walls.
A well-armoured coglin whose talents with machinery have been harnessed by the Ironbound order to repair and augment the many constructs that help guard the Vaults.

A brutish figure, hastily armoured in scraps of leather and metal to combat a fearsome intruder. On its back is an antique, arcane 'lightning rod', which calls down thunder on distant foes, although it cannot hit nearby targets.
A towering, muscular figure, capable of safeguarding its allies by selflessly accepting a portion of the injuries inflicted upon them.
A small canine scavenger. Packs of jackals roam the underworld, searching for carrion to devour.

A vampiric thrall bound into servitude by esoteric rituals. Though its rigid limbs give it an awkward gait, it moves with surprising speed, leaping upon its victims and leeching away their life essence with its vicious claws.
A spider spirit that takes the appearance of a human. It weaves deadly magics to incapacitate and kill its prey.
A gigantic humanoid with thick iron plates welded to its skin. It moves with alarming speed and deals incredible damage with its immense fists, but must rest between blows.
A spider which weaves webs between its front legs and leaps at its prey, ensnaring them. The speed with which it leaps is almost supernatural.
A giant bee, bearing a deadly barb which can sting repeatedly.
A comical figure full of life and laughter. It looks very happy to see you... but is there a slightly malicious cast to its features? Is that red face paint or something altogether less pleasant?

A humanoid construct of insubstantial memory, floating through the air. Though perhaps somewhat changed in shape and bearing few discernable features, still it seems somehow to resemble a warrior from the distantly remembered past, well equipped with arms and armour both.

A small, greyish creature with the look and temperament of a feral dog. No one knows for sure where kobolds come from, but ancient demon-gods, evil spirits, and meddling wizards have all been suggested as culprits.
A kobold that is bigger and tougher than the ordinary kobold, with a penchant for underhanded tactics.

A kobold, ready with multiple armaments to defend itself from the many dangers of the depths. The blastmote-packed cannon on its shoulder bears its maker's mark, and is fiercely loyal; it will fire for none other.
A kobold in league with demonic powers, able to call forth beings from the depths of Hell.
A skull-masked kobold, its body mutated by forbidden magics. It conducts vile experiments in the service of demonic powers, formulating ever more terrible monstrosities as vessels for devilish minds.
A wily kobold who has learned to weaponise every crack and crevice that lines the walls of its domain.
An enormous monitor lizard more than capable of preying on large animals.
A gargantuan sea monster, capable of devouring entire ships. Its many tentacles reach towards the shore and crush any who draw near.

A hideous conglomeration of mangled body parts, possessed and altered in ways that challenge sanity. Each varies in speed, strength, or resilience by the nature of whatever unfortunates were used to make it.
A blazing swift skull that cackles with the bleak malice of the dead. Fond of swarming, its laughter grows more spiteful and powerful for each nearby member of its own kind.
A burning red snake which dwells in pools of lava. It spits gobs of molten rock at passers-by.
An accursed soul magically bound to hellish servitude for the highest bidder. If its master is slain, it will be freed, departing this realm with gratitude.
A powerful wizard who has learned to cheat death itself, now existing as a skeletal, desiccated corpse kept intact by a mighty exercise of dark magic.
A buzzing contraption made from a coil and a rod. It irregularly zaps electricity at the most distant enemy in its range.
A small serpentine dragon with a pair of strong forelimbs. Its thick scales give off an eerie red glow.
A spell given ephemeral form, waiting only for a suitable target to enter its range. It will dissipate the moment it casts itself at a foe (or even if swapped with by an ally).

The echo of an unmourned soul. Though the memories of its living self are long-faded, it is drawn to the moment of death by some lingering instinct. It seizes upon the passage of other souls, losing the last vestiges of its being in the memories of another's life.

A formless mass of negative energy, bound to bring terrible torment once the forces holding it together dissolve. The alien presence of intruders to the Abyss is sure to unravel it, yet it seems perversely drawn toward them; still, it seems somehow reluctant to move while being observed.
A violet-scaled serpent with faintly glowing eyes. It thirsts for magic as well as flesh, and its bite can drink dry the magical reservoirs of even a powerful mage in no time.

A wooden theatre prop that moves as if possessed by a glimmer of another creature's skill and memory. It leaps to and fro with grace that is far from wooden, but its abilities often prove too much for its body - slowly falling apart with every action it takes besides moving. It refuses to acknowledge any instructions besides its own instinct.
A hideous cross-breed, bearing the features of a human and a lion, with great bat-like wings. Its tail bristles with spikes that can be loosed at potential prey.

The flame-wreathed skeleton of a carnivorous fish, darting through air as easily as it once parted water. It burns with a hunger it could not satisfy in life and is singularly driven by in death. While a single one may be only a nuisance, the swarm is never far behind, and every bite it lands will summon more and more of them until every scrap of flesh on its prey has been devoured.

The wandering shade of a long-dead soul who died for a forgotten cause. Though their memories have turned to mist, something deep within still compels them to serve and sacrifice - no matter the cost.

A nymphal hybrid, with a winged torso of a human atop the stinging abdomen of a bee. The meliai serve under many roles: priestesses of nature, nurses to the divine, and warrior-champions for their hives.
A hybrid with the torso of a human and the tail of a fish. It is capable of dwelling both in water and on land, and fiercely defends its domain.
A slender merfolk mystic with unusually webby hands. Its form shifts and glistens as if seen through ocean spray.
A beguiling merfolk whose voice mesmerises listeners. It carries no weapon, but its song summons drowned souls to defend the sea against intruders.
A powerfully muscled merfolk warrior, bearing a deadly weapon.
A fearsome merfolk champion with a piercing gaze and a large bundle of javelins.
A beguiling merfolk whose voice can mesmerise listeners.
A large muscular human with the head of a bull. It makes its home in a gauntlet where it awaits worthy challengers.
A hideous molten stone statue come to life, with flames licking across its body.

A flying munitions factory, held aloft on jets of fiery exhaust and packed to the brim with explosives. It can rapidly fill an area with bomblets, and when commanded by its creator, will explode them all (and itself) to devastating effect.

A serpentine crossbreed, blending traits of lesser dragons and countless other creatures that nature never intended to interbreed. Its many stunted limbs struggle to propel its grime-coated body, while its oversized scaleless head wheezes with the pressure of clashing breath weapons.

A multihued mire of roiling flesh and fluctuating sludge, striving and failing for more coherence than any other slime. As a fresh carrier of the ruinous contagion that overtook the Slime Pits, it can impart unto others the same horrible fate. While it may not be a permanent transformation for you, the melding of weapons and armour, as well as the severe weakening of spells, may make it a lethal one regardless.
A moth known for its ability to inspire rage by touching its foes, or merely gazing at its friends. For some inexplicable reason, it was eradicated from the surface centuries ago.

An enormous land tortoise whose shell is so thick and rock-encrusted that sleeping ones are frequently mistaken for geological formations. And like a mountain, its exterior is nearly impervious to any destructive force; only at close range can one properly aim for the narrow gaps between its plates to strike the tender flesh within.
An undead figure covered in bandages and embalming fluids, compelled to walk by an ancient curse. It radiates a malign aura.
An ancient servant of a long forgotten god, embalmed and cursed to walk in undeath for all eternity.
A bizarre creature, twisted and warped by overexposure to magical radiation. Each has a different set of traits.
A hybrid that is human from the waist up; below is a scaly, muscular snakelike tail. Its mouth drips with venomous saliva.
A naga that has trained in the use of magic, trailed by an eldritch nimbus. It is especially skilled in spells dealing with poison and venom.
An esoteric mystic draped in talismans. It venerates poison as a sacred gift and means of spiritual purification.
A naga with exceptionally keen eyesight, adept in the use of ranged weaponry and simple magics which allows it to snipe at targets across nearly any obstruction.
A fearsome naga warrior clad in sturdy armour and wielding a mighty weapon.
A magnificent example of the naga. It is an expert at both martial and magical arts.

A malign force from the space between planes. It is hostile to the magic forces that removed it from its home. These horrors are often the result of mistaken summoning spells and have slain many aspiring wizards.
A slime mold colony in an early phase of its life cycle. Not yet mature enough to reproduce, it can still defend itself by firing globs of potent acid.

An ancient stone creature that has lived among these frozen caves since before Antaeus rent Cocytus into being. It tolerates its new neighbors begrudgingly, preferring the company of its petrified enemies. Veins of ice permeate its frozen stone flesh.
An evil wizard who is devoted to the practice of death magic, the mastery of unholy energies, and the raising of corpses into a parody of life.
A vile undead creation of the most unholy necromancy, made from the decaying corpses of humanoid creatures. It exists to spread disease and decay.

An upright feliform trickster of an elderly demon, with a forked tail ablaze with a shimmering haze. It holds a deep disdain for mortal humanoids, a patronising pity for mortal cats, and enough mystic might to subjugate both.
A weirdly shaped demon, pulsing and shifting with mutagenic energies, its belly distended with the devoured brains of its victims.
A faceless stone bat unearthed from infernal chasms. Devilish beasts hunt in its wake.
A beautiful statue of an unknown creature, jet-black like a tear in reality. Its eyes glow with an otherworldly, malignant radiance.
A wizard fond of illusion and treachery. They scorn the crudeness of other magicians, who hurl wild conjurations toward their foes rather than cunningly exploiting their greatest weaknesses.
A more intelligent cousin of the mighty kraken, capable of using tools and spells. It is fully amphibious, but most of its species choose to stay beneath the waves and serve their King.
A large, ugly, and fat creature, distantly related to goblins. It is tremendously strong, and likes fighting alongside its orc friends.
A rare breed of ogre, skilled in the use of magic. It usually becomes a chieftain among its kin.
A very dangerous plant which fends off predators by spraying corrosive vitriol at them. Even experienced adventurers give oklob plants a wide berth.
A young oklob plant. It is more fragile than the mature specimen, but the acid it sprays is just as deadly.
A large, rowdy, and drink-loving creature. When they're not busy with their duties serving any number of gods, oni mostly love a good fight.

An infamous, dutiful retainer of Gehenna. These immense and indomitable oni weave their weapons through reality itself to reach and capture the innumerable damned souls owed to the hells upon their deaths.

A creature from the heavenly realms. It consists of a wheel within a wheel, and both of these are covered in eyes; strange flames of holy fire flicker all over it. To be seen by its countless eyes is to be highlighted and branded as both dissident and quarry for its allies to hunt down.

An intricately carved idol of some nameless godling, hewn of translucent orange crystal. Its lifeless eyes seem to glitter uncannily with a wicked intelligence. It is capable of unleashing a powerful psychic assault upon the minds of any who approach it.
An amber-coloured demon with a barbed tail not unlike that of a scorpion.

A huge, glowing, four-limbed purple creature with heightened senses, created by the Orb itself. It guards the Orb with enormous punctiliousness and violence, and its death will alert any Boundless Tesseracts on the level to begin creating reinforcements. Unless the Orb has already been disturbed, it will refuse to abandon its duty by leaving the floor.

A conjured globe of pure magic that homes onto a designated target, albeit with massive inertia. A smart and agile person may move out of its path, causing it to miss its target. It cannot be avoided by Dodging skill, and is able to make sharp turns to hit adjacent targets.
A globe of profound nothingness and the oblivion that awaits all things - flesh, souls, and even time itself. When the universe ends, only these will remain.
A globe of raw primordial fire, capable of impressive pyrotechnics and of twisting the very flesh of creatures who come into its ken.
A globe of deepest cold, still lingering from a time before the stars lit the heavens. It can shroud the soul in a chill so intense that even the gods cannot reach it.
An eerily glowing spider with strands of pure energy emerging from its spinnerets. It seems to want to keep its distance.

A subterranean tribe whose forebearers were once scattered across every corner of the surface world. Eons of persecution have taught them the necessity of violence and the importance of having your brethren at your side.

An orcish wayfarer who has been touched by the hand of Beogh. Whether out of religious devotion or personal jealousy, they have come to bar your path. Hold nothing back - for neither they nor their followers will do so. Glory to Beogh!
A favoured child of Beogh, once not so unlike yourself. Now that you have proven yourself to them, they will fight and die for both you and the cause. Shepherd them well.
An exalted servant of the orc god Beogh and a master of many foul rites, to whose aid Beogh will even send beings from the netherworld.
A heavily armoured orc, covered in scars from many past battles. It commands its brethren in battle, rousing them to greater, more violent efforts with bloodcurdling shouts.
A servant of Beogh, the ancient god of the orcs. Beogh rewards its devoted prayers by striking down its enemies.
An exceptionally competent orcish wizard, in league with hellish and chthonic forces and motivated by the purest imaginable strain of malevolence.
A supreme commander of an orc host, skilled at both melee and ranged combat.
An experienced, armoured and well-armed orc soldier, able to command a small mob of its fellows.
An orc who has gained proficiency in the occult arts, using them for martial purposes.
A muscular humanoid with pale scales, a reptilian tail and small wings.
A formidable demon lord inhabiting the endless halls of Pandemonium. Each one is different, with its own set of strengths and weaknesses.

A four-legged humanoid construct, tasked with recapturing escaped prisoners and punishing heretics. Long after the fall of the empire it once served, it continues to enforce imperial law, knowing no jurisdiction.
A dragon consecrated to the holy divine powers. Its breath is blessed fire, and its claws sear its victims with divine wrath.
A sizeable and statuesque flower, fossilised either by bitter grief or the cruel grace of divinity, standing in its own eternal vigil.

An intricate mechanical beetle covered in reinforced metal plates that resemble a shield. It projects a kinetic barrier around its creator while adjacent to them, increasing their armour class. It will never voluntarily leave its creator's side, and if forcibly separated, will prioritise returning to them over any other concerns.

A hideous translucent green spirit of a warrior fallen in battle but recalled to this plane by unholy magic. The blade it wields is ethereal, rendering those it strikes weak-willed and vulnerable to dark magic.
A nearly-transparent undead spirit, suspected by some sages to be a degenerate form of ghost, with no memories of its former life. It rarely stays in one place for long.
A royal ant returned to unlife through strange, probably horrifying means. It binds the souls of its allies when slain, allowing them to fight on after death as simulacra.
A heavily ruptured stonework, surrounded by rubble.

A leftover mess of broken bones, inert grasping organs, and scattered skin. While some highly-specialised sorcerers might be capable of bringing it to life, it is otherwise harmless - the possible leftovers of some departed or absent-minded magus.

A spire of strangely tenebrous ice, its brittle tendrils reaching skyward like the fingers of an outstretched hand. {{ if spells.memorised("rimeblight") then return "If only the dying breath of every soul could create such art." else return "It might even be beautiful if you didn't know the gruesome " .. "way it formed." end }}
A pillar of salt shaped like a statue, but worked by no living hands.
A plant that has adapted to grow in the unpleasant dungeon environment, somehow thriving even underground in the absence of the sun.
A gleaming warrior, wrought from precious metals and the very pinnacle of forgecraft techniques. Its every motion flows with a deadly, fluid grace that belies its artifical nature.

The apparition of an unfortunate adventurer, retaining many of the skills and abilities the adventurer had in life. It is condemned to haunt this particular level of the dungeons, lashing out violently at the next adventurer to cross its path.
A bear covered in glistening white fur, habituated to cold conditions. Like all ursines, it will become enraged if badly hurt.
A ghostly trickster that is fond of possessing small objects and making them fly noisily through the air.

Many poltergeists are fiercely territorial over the domains they choose to haunt, but these have extended that protection even to the people who share their domain with them. Some say they must be the lingering souls of those who guarded the Vaults in life; others suggest the Ironbound Order simply recruited them in common cause. Whichever is true, their very presence shelters other creatures from missiles, causing sling and spell alike to veer off-course at the last moment.
A blasphemous being that was once an angel of the Shining One. It now stands as unliving proof that not even the holiest of beings are beyond Yredelemnul's grasp.
A ravenous and incredibly buggy monster. Please report its existence to the DevTeam.

A gargantuan humanoid of fractured shape from the aeons when the seas were but primordial soup. The many shapeshifters of the dungeon once sloughed off from these unfathomably ancient beings, and when they themselves finally cease, even their remains will give birth one last time to furious monsters.
A starved spirit whose mouth is a pit of rot, emitting vile fumes. Its putrid maw cannot eat the food it finds, so it moans with rage and desparate hunger.
A muscular purple-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and small wings.
A ruler of a swarm of bees, even larger and more dangerous than its many offspring.
A long and sinuous dragon, seemingly more neck and tail than anything else. Its skin shines like molten mercury, magical energies arc from its pointed snout, and it moves with terrifying swiftness.
A mercurial spirit drawn from the elemental plane of earth. It exists in this world by inhabiting a shimmering body of liquid metal.
A pesky little marsupial that is a bit like a rat, but not quite.
A giant cockroach that has been exposed to high amounts of mutagenic energy. It is horrifyingly mutated, but this has only made it stronger.
A bedraggled priest, once-fine robes now lined with salt and dust. Forsaken by the gods, it now relies on constructs to protect itself.
A maneater demon, bestial and misshapen, in search of hidden power and knowledge. It is an expert in the art of illusion, and is exceptionally intelligent and cruel.
A dirty rodent that has grown large and aggressive in the dungeon environment.
A profoundly unnatural hound, crackling with electricity. It travels in packs, and covers great distances by bursting into living lightning.
A haunting form wielding a giant scythe, ceaselessly harvesting the souls of the living.
A larger cousin of the common imp, with a fiendish grin and two short wings sprouting from its shoulders. It favours tridents and loves to skewer its victims with painful barbs.
A muscular red-scaled humanoid with a reptilian tail and small wings.
A buzzing hornet with a vicious stinger dripping with paralytic poison.

A jet-black corvid with a nasty beak and a reputation for heralding bad luck. Most ornithologists consider this a baseless stereotype; the rest are still recovering from a series of staggeringly unlikely accidents.
A vicious black spider with a splash of red on its swollen abdomen. Its mandibles drip with lethal poison.
A crackling weapon formed of condensed magical energy. It can cut through entire rows of adversaries whenever its creator lands a melee attack.
The skeletal remains of someone who died unmourned and forgotten. It burns with an unquenchable hunger to be remembered.

A timeworn revenant whose flames dance with the silhouettes of long-forgotten atrocities. Cursed with a hunger they can never satisfy, they unleash these long-dead echoes to reenact violence upon any soul they deem worthy of adding to their eternal collection.
A giant annelid, glistening with slime, with unusually large teeth. It expels fragments of its own innards to ensnare unsuspecting prey.
A small but dangerous dragon. Its breath is visible even on the warmest days.
A rodent with hair of a most peculiar green colour, and a powerful bite. It tends to form great swarms with its kin.

A mutant sewer fish whose continuous exposure to wild magic has given it an appetite for magic itself. It swims through the air in a telekinetic bubble of the very sludge that gave birth to it, seeking out exotic prey from which to siphon novel magic.
A strange stone-scaled fish that swims through solid rock with the same ease that most fish do through water.
An oozing avalanche, scouring the ground beneath it as it rumbles forward. It consumes only the metal and bone from its victims, using them to reinforce itself even further.
A particularly rich and golden gelatinous thing. Smaller jellies swim and pulse just below its surface, ready to burst forth at the slightest touch.
An ancient pharaoh, embalmed and cursed to undeath, now capable of great and terrifying feats of magic.
A hideous humanoid figure with rust-spotted metal skin, spreading corrosion and decay to all it touches.

A slithering metal construct, once built to monitor for mutated entities encroaching upon the Vaults and long-since abandoned. While it can still dampen most unwanted magic, a lack of proper maintenance has led to its becoming coated with a highly corrosive mystic rust.

A large and vivid bloom drifting placidly upon the surface of the water. The cradle of the lotus's petals shine with eternity and elegance - while it is entirely harmless, it would take immense effort to destroy it.
A red, flaming half-human half-snake creature with a legendary affinity for fire.
A member of the salamander's scholarly caste, possessed of lesser size and strength, but wise in the ways of magic.
An intimidating volcano lord. It commands the magma of its realm as an extension of its body, and the majesty of its gaze can weaken even the proudest challenger.

A small, human-shaped agglomeration of salt. It was created by the last fugitive loyalists of the fallen eastern empire, forced in desperation to construct golems from local resources to defend themselves.
A more intelligent relative of the faun, often found in their company, and far more unforgiving of — and dangerous to — interlopers.
A loathsome arachnid, armed to the teeth. Its body is covered in a thick carapace, its tail is tipped by a venomous sting, and its forelimbs are equipped with a pair of sharp grasping claws.

A living engine of aquatic animal flesh fused with a colossal mass of bewitched metal scrap. Such hybrid terrors are perhaps the most successful experiments conducted in these tainted waters: its necromantically-attuned shell and a diet of furious drowned thieves has granted even this thrashing beast the ability to control the sunken souls of its countless victims.
A deeply unfortunate soul mostly processed into crystal by some malevolent tear in reality. Ethereal reflections of its past and future suffering are cast upon nearby surfaces and foes.
An irritable, bristling shrub. It fends off anything that might graze upon it by launching some of its innumerable toxic stinging hairs.
A brightly coloured snake, very comfortable in the water. It has a highly potent venomous bite.
An animated corpse alight with terrible fire. The flames are fueled by its regenerating flesh, which bubbles and melts as it grows.
A stubborn and fiercely territorial lizard with the strength of a mountain. Its thunderous footfalls herald violent tremors.

A lizard egg the size of a small boulder and nearly as hard. Perhaps as a defence mechanism, they hatch rapidly in the presence of predators and even a newborn can give all but the most ambitious of monsters a reason to consider an easier meal.
A six-winged servant of the good gods, of the highest rank of the angelic hosts. Its eyes burn with divine fire.

A member of an order of monks who abandoned their former faith. It now serves a minor god of wind and whispers, who allows it to calm the air and, when in great need, to break the stillness with divine thunder.
A hulking mutant swine who feasts like a king upon the abundant fungus of its realm and lords over its other denizens with brute force and unstoppable bulk.

A featureless silhouette of your own body, moving independently through the divine power of Dithmenos. No matter how many times it is struck down, it will reform itself, for a shadow is inextinguishable so long as whatever cast it remains.

A skulking apparition that disguises itself as a harmless shadow. Attuned to the dim light of the dungeon, it can slip in and out of sight at will, moving swiftly from one pool of shade to the next before striking unerringly at the blind spots of those who cannot see it.
A mysterious demonic figure, difficult to distinguish from the darkness around it. It weaves the shadows into powerful minions.
A great umbral dragon, radiating evil and death. Its breath reeks of the grave.
A shadowy minor demon, with an affinity for the necromantic arts.
A prism-like silhouette which wavers with barely-contained destructive energy. Any blow which disrupts its form will result in a violent blast of shadow.

A minor servant of living shadow whose form wavers perpetually on the edge of recognition - as if an unseen light were flickering behind something almost familiar. The strength of its attacks increases in proportion with the power of the spell which summoned it.

A strangely static silhouette whose form suggests a large cannon. Though it uses no gunpowder, the depths of its bore flickers angrily with every shot, as if remembering the fiery light of its ignition.
A mist-wreathed skeletal shadow, hanging in mid-air. It drains away the life force of living beings.

A gnarled mangrove, possessed of sapience and a cantankerous disposition. Its roots run deep through the water and soil of its marshy home and can make footing very difficult for those who provoke its ire. Marsh fauna are often found nesting within its branches, and may not take kindly to being disturbed.
A disturbing creature with the power to change its form. It is very rarely observed alive in its natural state.

An incredibly fast-moving bird, known for impaling its prey on shards of ice before tearing them to pieces. It has acclimated to the desolate wastes of Cocytus, and is enveloped with an accursed chill.
A strangely deformed floating eyeball, pulsating with flesh-twisting energy.
A sinuous serpent whose body crackles with volatile electricity. Its electric shroud can discharge when struck, inflicting a painful shock on any nearby foes.
A glimmering spark of magical energy. It seeks out nearby enemies to expend itself upon, dealing damage and pushing them backwards. It does not block its allies' line of fire.
A terrible spirit which brings an unearthly silence to the area around it, making it impossible to recite the magical incantations involved with casting spells or reading scrolls.
An icy replica of a monster, animated by heretical magics.
A small vile creature that moves in bursts, stopping then darting with lightning speed. It sprays sparks as it goes.
A vicious and heavily armed humanoid skeleton, animated by unholy power.
A skeleton compelled to unlife by the exercise of necromancy.

A strange aerial creature formed of fleshy clouds and electric feathers. It commands the faint wind currents of the Dungeon with every strike, which will buffet its victims in dramatic correlation to the amount of open air around said prey.
Skysharks cut through the air with a thoughtless ease. Just a taste of blood gives them an enraged strength, and further morsels drive them into a frenzy.

A surprisingly ambulatory mushroom. It wafts its spores over prey to send them into a deep sleep, making it simple for the fungus to kill and devour them. It can take months for its mycelia to fully infiltrate and digest victims.
An icky glob of slime that slithers along the ground. It can merge with other slime creatures to become dramatically more dangerous, and is especially likely to do so in confined spaces.

A quivering amalgam of viscous slime, its many pseudopods gnashing at the air like a throng of reptilian maws. It rapidly absorbs nearby slime creatures into itself, growing a new 'head' for each one and becoming even more resilient. Whether through convergent evolution or genetic memory, it also shares the hydra's most infamous trait: lopping off a head with a bladed weapon will just make it grow two more unless the wound is cauterised by a flaming weapon. When not stalking prey, its constituent slimes may separate from it again, perhaps to seek new food sources on their own.
A hideous mass of body parts. Each varies in speed, strength, or resilience by the nature of whatever unfortunates were used to make it.
An infernal demon that manifests itself as a writhing cloud of smoke. Having considerable pyrokinetic powers, it can very effectively attack its enemies from afar.
A swift and sinuous vine brought alive by a dryad's magic. It can quickly bind and entangle the dryad's foes, dragging them back to the forest from which it surges.
Part of a swift and sinuous vine brought alive by a dryad's magic. It can quickly bind and entangle the dryad's foes, dragging them back to the forest from which it surges.
A belligerent testudine with an armoured carapace. Its neck is surprisingly extensible and can reach out and bite from afar.

A mote of intense light and heat manifested by a sun scarab. It is linked to their essence and will never leave their side, being reconstituted time and time again whenever it is extinguished. Some myths even claim that the sun which shines down upon the outside world was once carried around by such a scarab.
A demon that manifests as a malignantly shifting shadow gliding through the air. It radiates an intense aura of negative force.

A tiny fragment of a living soul, splintered from the body in which it belongs. Too mindless to be fully controlled, it seeks nothing but to reunite with its greater self once more - unfortunately, this process tends to be more violent than the magic which created it.

A profoundly unnatural insect covered in vaguely metallic plates. Its stinger crackles with electricity, capable of delivering a powerful shock to unwary victims, and is capable of closing the distance with them at shockingly lethal speed.
A malevolent rift in reality, dissolving all terrain it passes by into swirling vortices.
A crazily shifting twist in the fabric of reality.
A spirit drawn from a weapon — it never strikes on its own. Damage done to it will be partially mirrored onto the caster.
A magical construct forged around a spark of its creator's own arcane power, allowing it to wield some of their destructive magics directly.

A wicked youthful hybrid with a woman's head, a lion's body, and the wings of an eagle. It gleefully wreaks havoc with both the violent turbulence of high winds and the frustration of bewildering magics.

A durable barricade made of ice reinforced with forgecraft magic. A lattice of precise hairline cracks are visible just beneath its surface which allow it to fracture into a barrage of razor-sharp projectiles whenever it sustains critical damage.
A small humanoid, resembling a human or elf except for the size. It moves at a great speed, and loves playing dirty tricks on people.
A magically adept spriggan blessed with the secrets of the winds.
A relatively mighty spriggan that plunges recklessly into combat.
An elite, well-equipped spriggan warrior, renowned for its unbelievable agility and its prowess with advanced weaponry.
A spriggan whose connection with the birds and the beasts is exceptionally strong. If it dies, its sacrifice will heal and temporarily strengthen nearby animals.
A spriggan that has tamed a hornet as its mount, and is tasked with protecting the spriggan fens and cairns from intruders.
A tarnished towering mess of half-assembled constructs and spare broken parts.
A white gelatinous mound that pulses with a strange iridescence. Its body absorbs magical energy like a sponge, and when sufficiently injured, will unleash this energy as a flurry of shooting stars.

A mass of stellar detritus that glows with the sickly putrescence of a dying star, forever shrieking soundlessly in a voice beyond mortal grasp. Its form undulates constantly, dividing spontaneously and then withdrawing when threatened. When divided, its deafening chorus of screams can overwhelm the minds of even the bravest warriors, leaving them stunned and helpless.
A mass of lashing vines and tentacles growing out of the husk of a dead star. Space itself runs through the xylem and phloem of its branches, which appear to be in many places at once.
The writhing appendage of a tentacled starspawn, capable of grasping nearly any prey and dragging it back to be devoured. Any damage dealt to it hurts the whole creature.
A sinuous length of an extended starspawn tentacle. Any damage dealt to it hurts the whole creature.
A piece of sculpted granite with glowing red eyes. Although it is rooted to its base, it can still move parts of itself.
A relatively small grey dragon, with a resilient-looking scaly hide and steam pouring from its mouth.
A large worm covered with hard, spiky metal plates. Despite the apparent heaviness of its outer armour, it is rather fast.
A mortal who made an unholy pact in life, now chained to tend the fires of hell in undeath as payment.
A gigantic humanoid with grey skin almost as hard as rock. It carries several boulders, and is perfectly capable of flinging them a great distance.
A powerful dragon with a hide of thick matte scales almost like blue rubber, and enormous scaly wings crackling with sparks.
A strange mechanical contraption, all hisses and pops. Shadows seem to dance across its reflective surface.
A demonic figure shining with the heat and fury of a fallen star.

A moth of transcendent beauty, coated in pyrophoric scales. Tiny cinders dance and twirl in its wake and whenever it beats its wings, they ignite in such spectacular displays of incandescence that one could almost forget how far away the sun is from this place.
A slimy dragon, its gnarly hide covered in swamp muck. Noxious gases dribble from its snout.
A small and slimy dragon, covered in swamp muck and giving off a terrible stench.
A large slimy worm, adept at traversing swamps and marshes.
A small but greatly-feared spider. Its touch alone causes victims to break into a frenzied dance.

Before even the oldest of ancient liches mastered life and death, a group of titans attempted to pull themselves free of mortality through brute strength. They almost succeeded before rot dragged them to Ereshkigal. A glimmer of their former beauty remains, alluring despite the stench.

An abandoned arcane experiment, its original purpose more inscrutable than most. Made of magical crystal fused with mutant brain tissue, it bobs about autonomously and erratically, sparking all the while. When badly damaged, it will unleash a staggering telekinetic shockwave, knocking back those in its surroundings and inflicting irresistible confusion on any who might harm it.
A humanoid figure with the head and talons of a bird. Its ferociously combative nature belies its fragile appearance.
A tengu with a talent for the destructive magical arts.
An elite, ferocious tengu highly skilled with both steel and spells.
A particularly bloodthirsty tengu who has opted to hone its skill in airborne fighting and weaponry instead of spellcasting.
The mighty tentacle of a kraken. Any damage dealt to it hurts the whole creature.
A part of the mighty tentacle of a kraken. Any damage dealt to it hurts the whole creature.
A writhing mass of tentacles, all covered in putrid mucus.
A lumbering maw shrouded in a mass of sinuous tentacles. On spotting prey, its tentacles lunge outward, dragging victims directly to its waiting gullet.
A seething mass of yellow flesh. It thrashes erratically, staggering foes beneath the weight of its impacts.
A huge, bolt-hurling, lightning-limned humanoid. It is unusually large and powerful, even among giants.
A clashing tempest of boundless energy, channelling into capacitor jewels. Its whirls of fire and ice occasionally escape and ricochet wildly off of walls.

A predatory marsh plant, possessed of motility and a rudimentary intelligence. It ensnares its prey in rings of spiny brambles and then skewers the trapped creatures with its razor-sharp thorns. When injured or approached by enemies, it can even raise these brambles as a barricade around itself.
A short-lived species of fungus typically found on or around decaying organic matter.
A huge animated statue made entirely from toenail clippings. Some people just have too much time on their hands.
A malign devil covered in all manner of claws, spines, and cruel hooks. It is able to inflict torturous agony on those foolish enough to gaze upon it.

A ponderous gastropod with a rock-hard shell. It is said to be in some way connected with the god Cheibriados; its very presence slows the movements of unwary adventurers, leaving them easy prey for its terrifying, ever-gnashing radulae.
A huge and physically powerful humanoid creature. Short on intelligence but long on brawn, its thick knobbly hide heals rapidly from most wounds.
A huge ogre with two heads on top of its bloated body. It is capable of holding a weapon in each giant hand.
An exceptionally aggressive blood-sucking annelid that thrives in swamps and marshlands.
A horrific fallen divinity, possessing jaws of gnashing stone and a necklace of starry organs. It spreads disease and despair, and patiently awaits the end of days when it will devour the sun.
A chattering and shrieking minor demon. They delight in sneaking past and backstabbing their prey.
A swirling tempest of souls and steel: knights and blacksmiths and weaponmasters, all bound to weapons they once held in life. To fight one is like fighting an entire army.
An ugly thing. According to legend, it is the otherworldly spawn of a wizard's breeding experiment. Yuck.

The Dungeon's vast repositories of the dead and the unholy realms thereafter both require regular restocking and reorganisation, far beyond the coordination of the restless dead. These corpse-collecting constructs burrow through the earth and command divisions of zombified hands to assist them in stealing away carrion, and may also violently create new corpses for such purposes.
A creature rarely seen by anyone; those few who have seen one would rather they hadn't. It moves erratically.
A funerary stone figurine kept in tombs to serve the deceased as they pass through the afterlife. It is inscribed with spells to protect the interred for eternity.
A human cursed with vampirism, drifting in a state between life and undeath, perpetually hungry for the blood of the living.
A large black bat with vicious fangs that feeds on blood. It is the preferred form for vampires in disguise.
A scornful scion to whom even other vampires bend the knee. Their command over blood magic allows them to feed upon the lifeforce of entire armies at once.
A powerful vampire noble who complements its combat prowess with dark magic.
A sorcerer who, by accident or design, has been afflicted with the curse of the vampire. Regardless, through undeath, it has finally mastered the art of dark magic.
A mosquito that has fed upon tainted blood and been transformed into a revolting and pestilent undead insect, seeking to drain its victims to the last drop.
A heavily armed and armoured guardian of the Vaults.
A vigilant scout, quick to alert its fellows to the presence of intruders. It marks such intruders with powerful magic, making them unable to hide from pursuit no matter where they flee.
A veteran commander, able to seal nearby doorways and staircases to prevent intruders from either trespassing further or escaping alive.
A very ugly thing. According to legend, it is the otherworldly spawn of a wizard's breeding experiment. Double yuck!
A bizarre symbiotic creature, made up of a carnivorous vine magically combined with a humanoid.

The viscous detritus of a thousand failed spells, surging forward with unnerving speed. Its very substance is a hole in the fabric of magic; enchantments find no purchase there and even momentary contact with it can leave one's spells greatly diminished.

A mobile and combat-capable alchemical manufactory that uses the friction of melee combat to brew a variety of useful potions. When it has built up enough heat to complete its synthesis, it will automatically dispense the finished potions to nearby allies and fall apart.

A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic, forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells. It is coated with impossibly ancient dust.

A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic, forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells. It is encrusted with long, sharp, deadly-looking crystals.

A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic, forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells. Its cover bears the icon of a long-forgotten god, still fully possessed of wrath.

A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic, forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells. It glistens with a thick layer of unmelting ice.

A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic, forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.

A large, fleshy mushroom that wanders slowly around the dungeon. It is both innately curious and incredibly shy, pursuing the objects of its curiosity only when out of sight. Noxious spores drift around its cap.
A particularly evil-looking wolf, usually found in the company of orcs.
A rare type of gargoyle, constructed from a solid steel statue and imbued with vicious strength, speed, and weaponised breath.
A spirit drawn from the elemental plane of water. It exists on this world as part of a body of water and can engulf other beings in its form, depriving them of breath and voice.
A largish venomous brown snake. It usually lives near water, and is an able swimmer.
A capricious nature spirit, deeply bonded with the waters in which it lives. Wherever they flow, so may it, and ponds and rivers surge and leap at its whim.
