You are covered with sticky fire, which causes damage over a moderate duration. Moving will quell the fire much more rapidly, and entering water will extinguish it immediately.
You are surrounded by light, greatly reducing your stealth and making you easier to hit.
There are barbs embedded in your skin, and moving around will cause you to take damage. Remaining in place for a short time will allow you to remove the barbs without taking damage.
You have been sickened, and your health will no longer regenerate.
You are disoriented and dizzy, reducing your accuracy, evasion, and spellcasting success rate.
You are corroded, reducing your damage in physical combat and your armour by an amount depending on the severity of the corrosion.
You are covered in illusionary wounds, causing severe damage while the effect remains active. Destroying the source of the illusion will restore all health lost to the flaying.
You are covered in ice, and your movement speed is reduced.
Your magic is sapped. Casting a spell will cause you to lose access to your magic, briefly preventing you from casting any further spells.
At least one of your strength, intelligence, or dexterity has fallen to 0 or below. You will act slowly until this situation is remedied.
You are channelling the dead, causing any living creatures killed in your vicinity to be raised as spectral servants.
You are divinely vitalised, providing protection from poison, confusion, petrification, and sickness, and increasing and sustaining your strength, intelligence and dexterity.
Your willpower is weaker, making you vulnerable to many magical effects.
You are petrified, and completely unable to act. You are very easy to hit, but all damage taken is substantially reduced.
You are turning to stone. Your actions are slowed, all damage taken is slightly reduced, and you will soon be completely petrified (gaining the Stone status).
You are more resistant to fire, cold, electricity, poison and acid.
Your wielded weapon or your fists are coated in slime, and will turn the next living or corporeal undead monster you hit into a neutral slime.

You are temporarily invulnerable to harm, but are brought close to death in the process and cannot be affected by healing while the effect is active. After the spell expires, it cannot be immediately recast.
You are still close to death's doorway, and cannot recast Death's Door for a short duration.
You are silenced. This makes reading scrolls, casting spells, invoking divine abilities, or shouting impossible.

Your lungs are filled with liquid, preventing you from breathing properly. This makes reading scrolls, casting spells, and invoking divine abilities impossible. You will also take asphyxiation damage every turn.
You are in the eye of a mighty ice storm. After the vortex fades, it cannot be called forth again for a short time.
You are surrounded by unstable winds, and cannot recast Polar Vortex for a short duration.
You are liquefying the ground around you, slowing the movement of all creatures in the area.
Your combat skills are temporarily increased.
You are duelling a foe in Okawaru's Arena, and will be returned whence you came if you are victorious.
You are destabilising space around yourself, causing nearby monsters to be randomly blinked away from you.

Your weapon is temporarily enhanced by the souls of the damned, providing slaying bonuses that increase with every enemy killed. At the maximum bonus, foes adjacent to your attacks' targets suffer pain damage.
You have lived beyond your means. You cannot spend gold again until you earn enough to cancel out your debt.
You are radiating toxic energy, and will continuously inflict poison on all nearby creatures.
You are reciting Zin's laws to nearby monsters, with a range of effects depending on the target. After finishing a recitation, it cannot be repeated for a short time.
You have recently finished reciting Zin's laws, and cannot recite again for a short duration.
You have targeted an enemy with a dimensional bullseye, causing missiles fired or thrown at a different enemy to also be teleported at the target.
You are calling a forested plane into temporary existence, and awakening nearby trees to damage your foes.
You are calling forth mighty dragons to attack your foes. Each dragon which answers the call will drain your magical energy. After the call ends, it cannot be issued again for a short time.
You have recently called forth dragons, and cannot recast Dragon's Call for a short duration.
You are terrified of nearby monsters, reducing your damage and accuracy in combat as well as the power of your spells.

You have +5 slaying and your melee attacks cleave. Your weapon also acts as though it had the {{return you.xom_bonus_brand()}} brand in addition to its normal brand (unless that was already {{return you.xom_bonus_brand()}}).
You are regenerating health and magic, but are also confused. Curing the confusion will also end the regeneration.
Your next use of an evokable device will have its power enhanced, at the cost of some of your magic.
A terrifying howl is echoing in your mind, calling forth powerful creatures to attack you.
Your body is covered in congealed blood, serving as armour for as long as you remain seriously injured.
You have been transformed into a monstrous, furry were-beast. The ferocious energy pulsing through your limbs keeps you ready to kill.

You are unstable at a fundamental level. You inflict dangerous levels of magical contamination on foes with each touch. Sufficient contamination causes a highly localised meltdown, dealing enormous damage. However, this instability makes you unable to use weapons, shields, or body armour. You also glow, reducing stealth and preventing invisibility, and you do less damage in melee, as your limbs sometimes destabilise mid-swing.
You have been transformed into a giant, cold-blooded, poison-resistant serpent, ready to wind your coils around foes and crush them to death.

Your midsection has transformed into a giant mouth, gnashing and ready to devour foes. The mouth may devour slain creatures, healing you to an extent increased by your Shapeshifting skill and the power of the creature eaten. Skill also increases the damage done by the maw.

You have been transformed into a slow but extremely robust stone statue. Your melee damage, both unarmed and with weapons, is substantially increased. Your stone body is immune to poison and miasma, and gains resistance to electricity, negative energy and torment.

{{ local desc = "You have been transformed into a mighty" if you.race():find("Draconian") then desc = desc .. " dragon" if you.race() ~= "Grey Draconian" then desc = desc .. ", increasing the power of any innate breath attacks" end if you.race() == "Red Draconian" then desc = desc .. ". You are highly resistant to fire and " .. "resistant to poison, but vulnerable to cold" elseif you.race() == "White Draconian" then desc = desc .. ". You are highly resistant to cold and " .. "resistant to poison, but vulnerable to fire" elseif you.race() == "Green Draconian" then desc = desc .. " and retaining your innate colour" else desc = desc .. ". You retain your innate colour, and are " .. "also resistant to poison" end else desc = desc .. ", fire-breathing dragon. You are highly resistant " .. "to fire and resistant to poison, but vulnerable to " .. "cold" end desc = desc .. "." return desc }} Your melee attacks deal incredible damage, and you are much more robust but less evasive.

You have been transformed into a lightning-filled tempest. Your melee attacks are strengthened and electrified, and strike all adjacent foes. You gain flight, increased evasion, immunity to poison, miasma, petrification, and constriction, and resistance to electricity. You gain the ability to launch yourself at foes as a lightning bolt.

You have been transformed into an undying offence against life itself. Foes struck by your hands or melee weapons are weakened, slowed, and drained, and you can heal yourself by tormenting living foes nearby. You also resist cold, have enhanced willpower, and are immune to poison, miasma, negative energy, and torment. Unfortunately, you are vulnerable to holy damage and Dispel Undead, and cannot consume potions.

You have been transformed into a swift-moving bat, increasing your evasion but substantially weakening your melee attacks. Any equipped weapons, armour and rings are melded, and you are unable to cast spells. The effectiveness of your melee attacks while in this form is based on experience level instead of on Unarmed Combat skill.

You have been transformed into a pig. You move quickly but are less effective in melee. Any equipped weapons, armour and rings are melded, and you are unable to cast spells. The effectiveness of your melee attacks while in this form is based on experience level instead of on Unarmed Combat skill.

{{ if you.race() == "Octopode" then return "A vicious spike has grown from one of your tentacles, " .. "increasing the damage of your extra tentacle attacks." else return "Monstrous horns or talons have grown from your body, " .. "granting a chance of making an extra attack in melee." end }}

You have been transformed into a banyan tree and are rooted to the ground, unable to move or teleport. You have minimal evasion but increased health and natural armour, and are resistant to poison, and immune to torment, negative energy, sleep, blinding, and do not need to breathe. Any equipped cloak, helmet, gloves, boots and body armour are melded.

You have been transformed into an insubstantial wisp of gas. You are highly evasive and are resistant to fire, cold, electricity and acid, and immune to poison, and negative energy. Any equipped weapons, armour and jewellery are melded, and you are unable to cast spells. The effectiveness of your melee attacks while in this form is based on experience level instead of on Unarmed Combat skill.

You have been transformed into a sentient fungus. You are highly evasive and can release spores to cause confusion when attacking in melee, but are unable to move when hostile creatures are present. You are resistant to poison and immune to negative energy. Any equipped weapons and armour are melded, and you are unable to cast spells. The effectiveness of your melee attacks while in this form is based on experience level instead of on Unarmed Combat skill.

You have been transformed into a swirling mass of dark shadows. You are permanently invisible and are immune to poison, draining, and torment. All incoming damage is halved, you bleed smoke on any incoming attack, and you have infinite willpower. However, your ability to deal damage in melee and with ranged attacks is halved, your spellcasting power is greatly hampered, and your maximum health is further drained when taking damage.

You are near (or perhaps holding) the Orb of Zot, whose energies disrupt translocation magic. Teleportation will take longer and scrolls of blinking may transport you a short distance away from your intended destination.

You are holding the Charlatan's Orb, whose energies disrupt translocation magic. Teleportation will take longer and scrolls of blinking may transport you a short distance away from your intended destination.
Your legs are tired, and you are unable to hop. This status will only recover after you spend several turns not moving. (Other actions, such as attacking or casting spells, are fine.)

You are currently channelling a ray of searing magical energy. Pressing <w>.</w> or <w>s</w> to wait in place will maintain and intensify the ray, at the cost of 1 MP per turn. Any other action, including recasting the spell, will end it.
You are moving at supernatural speed, causing movement actions to become instant. Any martial attacks made while moving in this way deal increased damage and never miss.

You are surrounded by a storm of heavenly clouds. While the storm rages, your evasion and combat accuracy and damage are substantially increased, and striking enemies with martial attacks increases this bonus. The storm weakens over time and fades away once the bonus reaches zero. The heavenly clouds prevent invisibility, and obscure the vision of those outside the storm.
Your movement is slowed on this liquid ground.
You are full of blood, and regenerate health quickly.
You receive spellcasting and slaying bonuses that scale with your health.
You can swear fealty to Beogh, the god of all orcs, through a nearby priest. To do so, use the Convert to Beogh ability in the ability menu.

Your body is entirely devoid of blood, reducing your maximum health and preventing you from regenerating health when monsters are visible. You are immune to poison and negative energy, significantly resist cold, and resist torment.
You are bribing the inhabitants of the current branch.
Your health and/or magic are being rapidly restored, as well as the health of your allies.
You are under both slowing and hasting effects.

{{ local verb = you.flying() and "flying over" or you.race() == "Merfolk" and "swimming in" or "standing in" local feat = view.feature_at(0, 0):gsub("_", " ") if feat ~= "deep water" and feat ~= "shallow water" then feat = "water" verb = "over" end return "You are currently " .. verb .. " " .. feat .. "." }}
Enemies are magically translocated toward you. (This won't wake them up.)

You have spent too much time in one branch, allowing the malevolent power of Zot to notice you. If you spend the indicated number of turns in the branch without descending to a new floor, Zot will find you, causing permanent health damage.
If you spend the indicated number of turns in this branch without descending to a new floor, Zot will find you, causing permanent health damage.
If you spend the indicated number of turns in this branch, its gem will be found and shattered by the power of Zot.
The power of Zot no longer hunts you, but this branch's gem still remains intact.
The wrath of Ignis prevents you from resisting fire.

You are unstable and cannot cast Blink or activate evoked blink abilities for a short period of time. Powerful sources of translocation magic such as scrolls of blinking ignore this limitation, as do external sources of blinking outside of your control.
You are recovering from becoming lightning, and are unable to blinkbolt again for a short duration.

You are currently channelling electrical charge. Pressing <w>.</w> or <w>s</w> to wait in place will maintain and continue this process until it discharges. Any other action, including recasting the spell, will dissipate the charge harmlessly.

You are currently channelling waves of flames. Pressing <w>.</w> or <w>s</w> to wait in place will maintain and intensify the waves, at the cost of 1 MP per turn. Any other action, including recasting the spell, will end it.
You are encasing nearby walls in ice. The ice will crack and fall away if you move to a new position.
You are creating a toxic bog in the nearby area, and are immune to its effects. You cannot sustain this transformation in areas out of your line of sight.
You are in touch with a greater truth, increasing your resistance to effects which target your willpower. Tragically, this epiphany won't last.
The dead are hopping! Living creatures you kill may rise as zombified servants.
You are peering down the stairs. You can freely return to the previous level, but once you take any action on this floor, all stairs leading back up will collapse.
Your body is as fragile and brittle as glass, increasing the damage you take from all sources.
Acidic ooze creeps out of the walls around you. Each turn, foes are damaged depending on the number of slimy walls they remain adjacent to.
Your canine familiar is recovering from its injuries, and cannot be summoned again for a short time.
You have recently siphoned the essence of the living, and cannot do so again for a short time.
You are fatigued from recently speaking a word of chaos, and are unable to do so again for a short time.
Jinxing spirits encircle you. When you attack foes, those who fail a Will check are jinxed, taking damage and becoming drained. The spirits depart quickly when no foes are in sight.
You are hovering upward toward the ceiling. After a short delay, Ignis' power will blast you into the level above.

You have been challenged by a chosen apostle of Beogh, who will know your location no matter where on the floor you are. Defeat them, and you may recruit them to join you. If you flee the floor, Beogh will punish you by temporarily depriving you of allies.
One of your apostles has been killed, and you have not yet killed all foes who were involved in their death. If you do so, Beogh will resurrect them sooner.
You have invoked divine aid in avenging the death of a fallen apostle. Orcs will continuously rally to your side, though your prayer will end more rapidly when there are no more foes around to fight.
An orcish apostle is available to recruit as a permanent companion. (Use the Recruit Apostle ability)

You carry the Black Torch. If this indicator is dark, the torch is unlit; if it is bright, you have called upon Yredelemnul to light the torch. So long as the torch burns, you will gain piety for kills. With sufficient piety, you will be able to use its umbral fire to empower your undead servants and damage your enemies.
Yredelemnul's grip is engulfing an area in life-stealing chains.
You're starting to limber up. Your weapon-based and unarmed attacks are closer to full strength, and will continue to grow more powerful with each swing.
You're limbering up. Your weapon-based and unarmed attacks are close to full strength, and will continue to grow more powerful with each swing.
You're limbered up. Your weapon-based and unarmed attacks are at full strength, and will remain so as long as you keep swinging and for a short while afterward.
Gravity around you is still unstable, and you cannot cast Gell's Gavotte again until it settles back down.
You are hurling conjured alchemical reagents at nearby monsters.
You are channelling the deepest night, greatly reducing your sight range. It will gradually return to normal over time.

Your vision is badly impaired. All spells and attacks you perform (which do not automatically hit) have an increased chance to miss. This chance is much greater the further away you are from your target.
You are marked with the sign of ruin, causing any melee attacks which damage you to heavily drain and randomly slow, weaken, or blind you.
You have not yet harvested enough death to cast Grave Claw again.
You are beckoning the legions of chaos; short-lived demons will be periodically summoned near you.
You have recently performed an infernal blood rite and must fully heal before being able to perform another.

You are sharing your body with an Executioner, giving you a powerful auxiliary attack that also triggers when you dodge attacks, as well as letting you rampage towards foes. This will expire quickly if you stop attacking.
Your Unleash Destruction is growing more powerful as you use it consecutively.
<Destr status> If you use it again, it will unleash a salvo of additional bolts aimed at random targets and this bonus will reset.
You are an instrument of Makhleb's destructive will. Your power and defences are greatly enhanced, but you must endure the Crucible of Flesh once this effect ends.

Makhleb has come to collect on certain promises made to them. {{ if you.religion == "Makhleb" then return "Fulfill your oath as their instrument by slaying the terrified " .. "mortals that have been gathered here, and they may grant you " .. "freedom once again." else return "Fight and bleed and you may be granted freedom once again." end}}
A path out of the Crucible has opened. Find it and claim your freedom again. For a time.
You are protected by a divine shield. Enemies that strike it in melee will have their attacks completely blocked, and they may also be blinded by its light.
You are preparing to unleash a kinetic shockwave and cannot move or be moved until this is complete.
You are winding up your clockwork bee. It cannot attack its target until it is fully wound up.
You have become untethered in space, blinking randomly each turn and suffering a small amount of damage each time you do so.
You have recently announced your regal presence and it simply would not do to leave the floor again so soon afterward.
Your platinum paragon is close enough to you to sometimes parry attacks directed at you.
Your mind is clouded by frustration. For the next several turns, you will uncontrollably attack random adjacent creatures (whether friendly or enemy) or even empty space.
You are rapidly growing sleepy and may soon fall asleep completely.

You are a vampire - a creature that straddles the border between life and undeath. You can drink the lifeblood of the living to heal, and even turn those you slay stealthily into vampiric thralls, but do not heal in the presence of monsters.
You have transformed into a swarm of vampire bats, allowing you to move quickly and evasively. You may trail clouds of bats in your wake.
This indicates how many spells you could cast from accumulated memories if you Enkindled now.

You are burning accumulated memories for power. Each damage-dealing spell you cast will consume a memory. In exchange, their power and spell success are increased, encumbrance penalties are ignored, and your spellclaw attacks do bonus damage proportional to the spell level and heal you based on the damage dealt.

You are noisily attacking with all of your armour. Every piece of armour you haunt currently moves of its own volition; any damage it takes will not affect you, you can freely fire through it, and its attacks may daze, drain, or confuse your enemies.

You have an explosive catalyst readied. The catalyst will detonate, dealing fire damage to the primary target of each of your melee attacks and any enemy adjacent to them, with each hit. Attacking will extend the duration of the catalyst even if you miss.
You are covered by a thin shroud of slime that may deflect a melee attack. When it does, the shroud will break for a short time, though it will soon repair itself naturally.
You are a rime yak, fur encrusted with ice.
You are an agile jumping spider whose attacks can web enemies.
You have spiny quills growing out of your body which may damage melee attackers.
You are a living beehive, abuzz with busy insects.
The insects that dwell within you have recently swarmed to your defence. This will not happen again until your health fully recovers.
Your body is composed mostly of elemental water that can reach to attack and drown enemies.
You are a cunning, riddle-loving sphinx, with the force of a windstorm in your paws.
The damage and accuracy of your attacks is temporarily increased.
You are a walking scroll, parchment crisp and full of magic.
You are a heavily-armoured crab with rusting breath.
You are a sun scarab, with solar fire blazing beside you.
You have a mane of venomous tendrils for hair.
Your lithotoxin has recently activated and will not do so again until you fully heal.

A malevolent fate is gathering around you. If your Doom reaches 100%, you will be afflicted by a random bane and your Doom will reset to 0. Banes have diverse negative effects that can significantly endanger your character for an extended period of time. Both Doom and Banes are only cured by gaining experience, though Banes typically last much longer.
Your connection to the divine has been partially cut-off, temporarily reducing your effective piety. Gaining experience will eventually recover all piety that has been locked away this way.

A Boundless Tesseract is drawing in forces from a parallel reality. New monsters will steadily appear at random locations across the floor until either of the tesseracts is destroyed. If this is allowed to continue for a very long time, those monsters may sometimes appear near your location instead.
Your orb of stardust has recently expended its energy. It will recharge once several turns pass while your MP is full and there are no enemies in sight.
Your orb of mesmerism has recently expended its energy. It will recharge after a short length of time (but cannot recharge on turns where you move).
Your claustrophobia has given you a slaying malus. This is dependent on the number of walls surrounding you.
The power of all your spells is reduced by half.
Your next attack will have increased accuracy, inflict three times its normal damage, and cleave at an increased range. This bonus is lost if you perform any action besides attacking.
Your evasion and slaying are increased. This stacks up to 3 times and will never expire so long as you continue to perform melee attacks.
Your body is slowly being turned into slime. Even if a full transformation occurs, you have enough force of will to eventually revert back.

You have been temporarily transformed into a jelly. You have several unusual resistances and extra health, but heavily weakened spells. Any equipped weapons and armour are melded. The effectiveness of your newly-acidic melee attacks while in this form is based on your experience level rather than Unarmed Combat skill.
You are covered in regenerative ooze from your recent trip down the stairs. For a brief time, your wounds will heal rapidly and your reserves of magic will recover quickly.
You are unable to cast Hellfire Mortar again until the effect of your last cast ends.
Your maw has just consumed a delicious meal, greatly increasing your regeneration until it finishes digesting it.
Multiple vicious blades are growing out of your body.
Your arm is a mass of multicoloured fungus.

You are stampeding forward. Any movement you take into an enemy will trample them backwards, but your stampede will end as soon as you perform any action {{ if you.mutation("East Wind's embodiment") > 0 then return "besides rampaging, stampeding, or casting spells." else return "besides rampaging or stampeding." end }}
You are rapidly regenerating health (at a rate dependent on your max HP) until you have healed the specified amount.
Your next several ranged attacks will cause you to fire a flurry of additional shots at other targets in sight.
Your next Rampage movement will be instant.
You have recently used Divine Exegesis and may repeat the same spell you can this way at a greatly reduced piety cost.
You have recently discharged a full-power jolt of electricity and cannot do this again until you fully heal.
You have recently cast Sirocco and cannot cast it again until you spend several turns without moving.
Your third eye is open, allowing you to see the magical energy left over from spellcasting and convert it into damaging projectiles.
A mass of elemental crystal shrouds your upper body, granting you increased skill with elemental magic and the ability to unleash it in a powerful burst.
You are a hypnogecko, a stealthy lizard who can shed their own tail as a decoy when badly injured.
You have recently shed your tail and need to explore more of the dungeon before it can grow back again.
Your body is insubstantial, granting you immunity to constriction, petrification, barbs, sticky flame, webs, nets, and being caught by bolas.
A gaseous mixture from a recently-consumed potion swirls within you. Your next melee attack will spew clouds based on the type of potion that was quaffed.
Your head is a cloud of swirling mist. Any potions you drink will be metabolised into clouds of baleful gas which you can expel with your melee attack.
The reach of your melee attacks is increased by 3.
All of the stairs on this floor have been sealed. You must kill a certain number of enemies before they will be unlocked again.
You are rapidly losing patience and will soon go berserk.
When moving towards enemies in a straight line, you cover any distance in a single step.
You are hurling pebbles at all foes in your line of fire.

You have been granted temporary knowledge of a single spell, which you can cast at the cost of magic contamination (proportional to the spell's level and reduced by your own experience level) using the Eisegesis ability.

Xom has granted you a persistent ally, which will accompany you between floors and eventually be revived after dying. It is also immune to your attacks and can be freely shot through. After dying a large number of times, it may lose much of its power.
You can rampage quickly towards monsters, and when you do, you spend 1 MP per step to create a living beam spell in your trail.
Slaying corporeal foes yourself will cause Xom to gift you mannequins in their image once the battle is ended.

A chaotic battleshape will appear next to you in combat, firing when you attack in melee and detonating when you cast a spell while it is fully charged. If it is destroyed, it will rematerialise again after a short time.
When injured below 60% of your max HP, aspiring flesh will burst from your body, eventually transforming into short-lived but powerful allies.
Aspiring flesh has recently burst from your body and cannot do so again for a short while.

All of your stab attacks deal damage as though you were wielding a short blade and whenever you would be first noticed by an enemy, you will instead disguise yourself as an unremarkable object, allowing you to avoid detection for a brief while.

You are cleverly disguised and completely unnoticeable to enemies. You will always succeed at distraction stabs, but your disguise will end as soon as you attack, cast a spell, use an ability, read a scroll, or evoke an item. It will also end on its own after a short duration. If all enemies who were in sight when you donned the disguise are dead when it ends, and there is nobody else around to see you, its cooldown will be skipped.
You have recently disguised yourself and must explore some more before being able to do so again.
An amulet to be worn as jewellery around the neck, charged with arcane powers of unknown provenance.
An arcane textbook containing magical spells of unknown origin.
An unlabelled flask containing a single dose of unknown liquid.
A ring charged with arcane forces of unknown provenance, to be worn as jewellery on a finger.

A disposable arcane formula inscribed on parchment by a professional scribe or sorcerer. Anyone can evoke the power of the arcane formula by reading it out loud, but the nature of that power is not a priori apparent.
A staff improved with arcane powers of unknown nature.
An enchanted blade which loves nothing more than to sing to its owner, whether they want it to or not.

A bloodstained axe that was the favourite weapon of the old god Trog, before it was lost. It induces a bloodthirsty berserker rage when used in battle, although mere mortals who wield it will find themselves temporarily overwhelmed by Trog's power.
A large mace said to have appeared when Xom grew bored with the predictability of more ordinary instruments of chaos.

The partisan of Prune carries a terrible and insidious curse. Unless its wielder maintains firm self-control, they are doomed to undergo a horrifying (albeit temporary) transformation. This is normally trivial to resist, but incapacitated wielders are certain to succumb, finding themselves nightmarishly purple, squishy, and delicious. They can take comfort in learning that it's surprisingly hard to injure a giant prune.
A staff which was once wielded by the great alchemist Olgreb.

A sphere of flawless crystal, shaped by countless mantras. When one focuses upon it, the boundaries between 'self' and 'other' sometimes seem to blur. {{ if you.race() == "Djinni" then return "It is utterly useless to Djinn." end }}
An ivory-like quick blade that looks like it could have been crafted from the tooth of some enormous predatory creature. It is lethally vampiric.
A scythe surrounded by an ominous aura of dread. It carries a terrible and ancient curse, which it busily inflicts on both the wielder and their enemies.
An accursed bone sceptre, created by some unknown hellish power. When used in combat, it causes agonising pain in all those unfortunate enough to gaze upon it, save for the wielder.
A twisted blade, covered in eerie flames. Its demonic power burns away at the very essence of those it is wielded against.

An orb pulsing with unholy energies, granting the power to unleash damnation when held — although not without draining the wielder's vitality in the process. It carries with it some of the corrosive malice of the Iron City of Dis.
A bright ruby sceptre, carrying some of the powers of the arch-fiend Asmodeus. It may call forth fiery demons from their infernal home to do the wielder's bidding.

An enchanted suit of armour created from the scales of a rare breed of dragon, now thought to be extinct. This prized relic is now one of the last proofs that the vividly coloured faerie dragons ever existed.
A blade forged in Hell by the sacrifice of countless tortured souls. It inflicts the rage and suffering of those souls upon its wielder.
A scimitar with a mysteriously smoking blade. Occasionally its heat leaks out, covering opponents in magical flame.

Soon after falling, Yredelemnul attempted to twist holy energy into a dark mockery of itself, turning it against its progenitors and weakening it against undead and demons. It was discovered too late that such a complete perversion was uncontrollable; the foul flame destabilised or destroyed everything it was infused into, except for several demonic test subjects and one stolen holy weapon. A lesser, and more stable, version of the dark energy proved more workable, and became Yredelemnul's umbra. This is that weapon: an eveningstar with its light long fled, despite its name, and a shadow that repulses those its light used to comfort...

A blade forged in Hell by the sacrifice of countless tortured souls. It fills its wielder with the rage and suffering of those souls, and gorges itself further on drained life force every time it strikes, leaving behind a mess of blood and gore.
A dagger made of one huge shard of sapphire. It covers opponents in ice, slowing down their movement somewhat.
An ugly rusty dagger. Many years ago it was the property of a powerful mage called Boris. He got lost in the Dungeon while seeking the Orb.

A long and exceedingly sharp scythe, capable of eviscerating in a single blow. Its extraordinary speed is the work of a mad wizard, who spent years refining it before discarding it in a fit of rage. The blade looses a low keen as it cuts through the air.
A sling made of weird green leather, oozing corrosive slime. Originally the weapon of a notorious mischief-maker and general scamp, it's since fallen into less savoury hands.

A golden bow, strung with a lock of hair from the West Wind themselves. Tales say it was crafted as a gift to an unrequited love and even centuries after their untimely death, one can still feel longing carried on the gentle breeze that surrounds its wielder.
A massive enchanted cudgel that augments the already considerable strength of anyone mighty enough to wield it.

A glaive commissioned several years ago by a wealthy queen fearful for the safety of her vast treasury. No foe, the smith promised, could defeat a guard wielding such a weapon! It was stolen a few months later, along with the rest of the queen's treasury; the guard, it transpired, had been caught napping. Still, it should serve more than adequately in the hands of a waking user.

A sword made of one huge piece of crystal. Legend says it was the Shining One's gift to a worshipper. This blade is notorious for inducing bloodthirsty rage in both the wielder and all of their followers.
An unholy crossbow, forged in the fires of Gehenna. It imbues the bolts it fires with the raw power of its namesake. Thankfully, the blasts this weapon produces never harm the one firing.

An adamantine great sword. Its first wielder was a worshipper of Yredelemnul who eschewed the use of magic in combat, preferring to destroy her enemies with brute force. Unfortunately for her, not all of her opponents shared her limitations. It has felled countless great warriors under her grip, and the souls of those who had their lives taken beckon it to take even more under its new owner.
A jewelled morningstar, glowing brightly with the light of the dawn. It illuminates the dungeon's recesses, revealing the machinations of those who would prefer to stay invisible.
A dark and malign artefact. It increases the potency of hexes cast by anyone unwise enough to risk wielding it.
A trident stolen many years ago from the Octopus King's garden. Luckily, he seems to be in no hurry to get it back.
A beautiful mithril axe, probably lost by some dwarven hero.
A powerful staff which used to belong to the leader of the Guild of Five Elements. It is imbued with protective and offensive enhancements from all the elemental schools of magic.
The sacred weapon of Toth-Mos, first apostle of the god Ashenzari. It grants the wielder a fraction of Ashenzari's own vision, ensuring that every shot will land true.
This blowgun seems to guide the needle to seek the most lethal point to hit the target, packing a nasty punch.

An enchanted lance deadly to all dragonkind. It grows more powerful every time it inflicts a killing blow on a strong dragon. The more powerful it grows, the harder it will be to find a worthy opponent.
A dainty little knife which was made by Spriggans, or for Spriggans, or possibly from Spriggans. Anyway, it's in some way associated with those fey folk.
A triple sword made of weird glowing metal. It irradiates those it strikes, causing a range of unpredictable effects — if they survive the impact of the blade itself, that is.

A weapon imbued with magic to disrupt and destroy the forces binding undead creatures together. Legends say that, long ago, a lich lord created many such weapons to ensure the loyalty of his undead servants. Sadly, this mace might be the last one left.
A double-ended whip made from the cured hides of black mambas, and enchanted with toxins ranging from ordinary venoms to asphyxiating curare.
Presumably this relic led to the invention of the famous spell, or maybe the other way around.
An infamous weapon, once used by a vile pirate captain to slaughter countless innocents. He finally met his destiny when a kraken swallowed his ship, and the cutlass was thought to be lost with him.
A longbow with the colour of dark rain clouds that fires arrows like lightning.

A shield unearthed from the remains of a ruined city. It bears an inscription written in an ancient language. Scholars and wise men laboured for countless hours to decipher it, and in time, a translation was finally settled on: "With a shield like this, who needs to think?"

A variegated robe, woven with enchantments to enhance the wearer's physical and mental abilities. Its creators wove in strands of hair from a hundred different animals, each chosen for the unique strengths it could grant the robe's wearer.
A pitch-black cloak which allows its wearer to excel in the arts of thievery. Even the clumsy will find their footsteps softer and the shouts of their adversaries less attention-getting.
Just in case you had trouble getting hit.

A large circlet of dull bronze, set with a dazzling array of gemstones. It was first worn by a prince of the Titans, who sought protection from the incessant warfare between his fellow princes. In practice, the main effect of the artefact was to unite his rivals against him.
A fur hat once owned by Ukta, a powerful ogre shaman. It houses the spirit of an especially mighty bear, whose rages devastated the ogres until it was slain.
A splendid flowing robe of fur and silk whose lucky colour has faded.
A cloak that twitches and jerks without any intervention.
A soft hood, enchanted by members of the Assassin's Guild to allow the wearer to sense potential victims nearby, and to easily spot vulnerabilities after closing in on them.
A well-made golden hauberk that covers all of its wearer's body parts. It includes a chainmail coif, chausses and maille gauntlets.
The {{ if you.can_smell() then return "smelly " end }}skin of some strange animal, native to cold and distant lands. It radiates the chill of its native habitat.

Most salamanders' bodies are consigned to the fiery depths from which they sprang. Rarely, though, salamanders instead preserve the skins of those that passed. The runes and decorations on this hide suggest it once belonged to a respected warrior or priest - perhaps even a king. The fiery spirit remains in the skin, granting its power to the wearer.
A pair of thick steel gauntlets. They were Okawaru's reward for a mighty warlord. The owner is destined to die in battle, but what a death it will be!

A bronze shield, looking almost exactly like a tortoise's shell. It was built by the adherents of an obscure minor faith, who imbued it with the power of their god. As the god is said to, this shield protects against sword and sling, frost and flame.
A dull grey robe. It is enchanted to provide mages with immeasurable power, and more than a little overconfidence...

A suit of armour created by the famous inventor Maxwell, providing unparalleled protective qualities at a very affordable price. His unorthodox materials left it with certain shortcomings, but he's yet to have anyone come back for a refund.

The mask of the High Priest of ancient Erebora. In ancient times, the gods of the Ereborans ceased to answer their prayers, and in desperation, the people turned to the forbidden worship of dragons. Now, of their works, only this mask remains.

A long black robe made of strange glossy material. It shrouds its wearer in darkness, reducing the range of vision. According to legend, it was the gift of Rutra, a renowned demigoddess of the night, to one of her followers.

A suit of armour created from the enchanted scales of a once-mighty king of dragons. In his time, titans and lesser dragons struggled with him in vain — but as with all things, even he was eventually cast down and undone. Of his life and deeds, this is all that remains.
A dirty hat. It bears signs of surviving many weird explosions, which suggests it may have means of protecting the head inside from the risks involved with alchemy experiments.
A phosphorescent cloak, woven of pure light beams. The ripples of its folds as the wearer leaps and swerves in combat may dazzle those who gaze on it.

A cloak stitched from the hides of hundreds of hell rats by an enchantress with far too much time on her hands. Many more rats remain somehow concealed within it, and may scurry out to assist the wearer.
A heavy bronze gong that can be worn as a shield. Locked away in a temple for many years, its bearer is shielded by decades of accumulated prayer.
A sky-blue amulet, suffused with enchantments that protect the wearer and make their Air spells more powerful. Its creator lacked just one thing: a steady hand.
A black ring that can make its wearer one with the shadows.
A strange-looking piece of crystal on an ordinary-looking string, with an odd selection of powers.
A pendant made of purest jade. It grants its wearer immense willpower and mental fortitude.
A necklace made of bloodstained human and animal teeth, and something that appears to be a piece of spine.
An unadorned malachite ring, half of an ancient pair. Its wearer is exceptionally difficult to catch.
A rough-hewn aquamarine ring, half of an ancient pair. Its wearer is exceptionally difficult to harm.
An enchanted sapphire, inset into a ring. It aids the spellcasting of its wearer.
A brooch with an intricate inlaid design, providing a range of magical protections. Back in the good old days, every adventurer had one of these handy devices. That, and a pony.
A robe of a material as nebulous and insubstantial as the clouds. It whips the air around it up into a furious storm as it ripples and swirls.

The favourite hat of the slug wizard Gastronok, stained with reddish slime and enchanted to aid in his arcane pondering. It has been specially enchanted to protect against the desiccating effects of salt.

An axe with a powerful curse placed on it by one of the lords of Pandemonium, so that unsuspecting adventurers would unleash demons into this world. Beware, for it has ways of mesmerising its wielder, no matter how clear and focused their mind...

An axe with a delicate blessing placed on it by one of the sacred Seraphim, so that worthy adventurers would rid this world of demons. Rejoice, for it has ways of bringing courage to its wielder in even the darkest places...
A set of armoured plates assembled to protect a creature with a long, scaly lower body. Faintly crackling with electricity, they supercharge their wearer's ability to cover distance.

A heavy barding made from pitch-black steel and inlaid with plates of black diamond. It once protected the steed of the Black Knight during their reign of terror. Those who wear it become partially undead, gaining some of the benefits without the unfortunate downsides, although the great weight of metal and stone slows the wearer somewhat.

A jewelled amulet famed for its powers of resilience and recuperation. Its greatest notoriety came from its use by the dread necromancer Borgnjor, who relied upon it to maintain her slender hold on life. After her final demise, the amulet vanished from the pages of history.
An exquisitely crafted sword. Its blade is so sharp that it can cut through space itself.
A wooden cudgel, loaded with more than just lead.
An opalescent cloak gleaming with the colours of all kinds of dragons. It imbues the wearer with draconic resistances, although somewhat unreliably.
One of the eight rings once worn by the Octopus King and now scattered across the land. Each has its own unique enchantment.
As you hold this axe your mind does not feel fully your own. Your body begins to exhibit strength far beyond its capabilities, and your movements become guided by Makhleb.

A suit of armour rumoured to have been created by enchanting the hide of a now-extinct species of troll. Whether the name rings true or is merely appropriated to add mystique is something of a mystery. The armour's innate powers of regeneration and magical protection, however, are hard to dispute.
An ugly dangling finger on a string. Everything about it reeks of malign influences... but it's hard to avoid thinking that it would look better with a ring on it.
A novel pair of boots invented by a suitor of Arachne.
A large, iron-shod maul specialised for dealing massively powerful blows. Such power comes at a price: the maul's head is so heavy it takes a great length of time to lift it up for another swing.

A relic of some ancient wizarding war. Centuries later, it still crackles with effects from the residual hexes and magical energies it was once subjected to on a daily basis; spellcasters able to get a handle on its power, however, will find it enhances the power of their spells.
A blade somehow crafted from pure electricity. It arcs wildly between the wielder and their foes as it strikes.
A weapon said to have once been used to keep unruly imprisoned wizards in line; it violently disrupts the flow of magic around it.

A silver-bladed lajatang, once bestowed upon a favoured worshipper of Zin. It became the most prized weapon of the many priests of Zin. After their order was destroyed, it fell into disuse and vanished from history.
A huge mace imbued with potent fire magic. It fills those it strikes with an inner flame, and offers some protection against the resulting devastation.

A suit of armour carved from transparent orange crystal. It provides remarkable protection for both mind and body. The wearer can even channel psychic energies through the crystal itself, enhancing their magical abilities. However, it's rather heavy...

A staff inhabited by a mighty demon, tricked and trapped in this form long ago. To survive, she now offers great arcane power in a terrible bargain: in exchange for a tiny portion of the caster's life essence, taken every time its wielder casts a spell, she will redirect the life essence of creatures damaged by the spell to the caster.
Two quick blades joined by a chain. Swinging one compels the wielder to swing the other, as if they have minds of their own.

A fine mesh cage designed to capture magical energy. Experimental notes suggest that research was abandoned when the cage began to capture magical contamination almost as effectively. Anyone reckless enough to place it on their head would find their magic regeneration dramatically increased, at the cost of multiplying any magical contamination received.
A gold crown set with jet-black gems. It permanently afflicts its wearer with agonising pain, substantially reducing their resilience but rendering them immune to further torments.
A robe woven of living vines. The vines form a symbiotic relationship with their wearer, greatly increasing their regeneration, but preventing them from being healed by potions.

A coat of armour said to have been forged for Queen Kryia in her old age. She continued to insist on leading her armies from the front even into her dotage, and as her aging body failed her, this coat helped to enhance the healing draughts that kept her alive.
A massive axe that looks like it was carved from a glacier, or possibly calved from one. It leaves ice crystals in its wake as it swings through the air.
A huge and weighty suit of bronze plate armour. Only one with a correspondingly huge body can wear it.
A handheld array of hexagonal mirrors, synthesised from a truly exotic substance and polished to a blinding sheen.
An amulet that can be activated to render its wearer invisible.
A scarf that can be activated to render its wearer invisible.

A strange sword, one blade blistering hot and the other icy cold. When it hits its target the thermal gradient increases. What causes this effect is unknown but it is rumoured that otherworldly forces are involved.
A small wrinkle in the very fabric of reality, magically bound to a shaft by some mad acolyte of Lugonu. Its attacks can warp through nearby space at the wielder's command.
An orb encased in vividly coloured scales, wrought by a long-forgotten wizard. It was the mage Iskenderun's favourite playtoy.

A suit of armour borne of rotten flesh and bone and gristle, held intact by the will of a long-dead sorcerer. The dreadful energies within it call to the bodies of the recently dead, protecting the wearer with a cocoon of carrion.
An enchanted pair of boots which grant the ability to take strides of incredible length, as long as the wearer is advancing bravely towards their foes.

A pair of gloves designed to carefully control and channel the flow of magic, later misused and mangled by the lunatic murderer-mages of the Fifth Circle. Their influence leaves the wearer utterly unable to cast spells - the wearer's magic is redirected to far bloodier purposes.
A dull dusty mixture trapped within a cracked crystal on a thin silver chain.

A beautiful rainbow of colour and motion trapped within a delicate crystal on a thin silver chain. Listening carefully, one can hear the distant echo of a thousand dreams from all corners of reality, their melody giving a warm sense of safety.

A pair of long ultramarine gloves, worn by a famed experimental alchemist in an age long past. They channel the energy of discovery, empowering their wearer with the force created by a blind step from ignorance to certainty.

A weapon that chops foes down as steadily and methodically as a forester cutting wood. The unchanging rhythm of its work has settled on it with the force of natural law, and no amount of force or skill can make it swing faster or slower.

Taken from a paladin of the Shining One by the common cutpurse who murdered her, Throatcutter was used for a long series of increasingly sordid deeds thereafter. Blood, murder and betrayal stain its history and blade both, and little trace now remains of the blade which once stood between danger and the innocent.

A sacred relic of the Monks of St. Lee, followers of the renunciate archmage. Just as St. Lee sought to atone for the destruction his spells wrought by protecting others, so his staff protects its wielder.

A weapon to bring forth guilt from the guilty. It was first wielded by the archangel Lucriel, who, on seeing the suffering of the first mortals, led them as an army against the cruelty of the gods. The ragged survivors of Lucriel's army took this weapon with them into the wilderness, the sole remnant of an archangel's virtue.

A blue-steel amulet. Its creator, an exceedingly practical woman, designed it to provide powerful protection against mundane jabs, stabs and bites. It's worse than useless against fire and frost, but how often does anyone really need to worry about that?

These sturdy boots were created by an artificer who lived high up on a remote mountain peak, as protection against the mountain's near-constant avalanches, rockslides, and snowstorms. No force short of translocations magic will budge the wearer from their position.
This brutal weapon, long thought lost to history, combines the extended reach of a polearm with the cleaving sharpness of an axe. Ghosts of ancient warriors linger about it, draining fickle users.

An ascetic once took a sacred vow, forswearing use of magical tools and ownership of everything but this pendant. Which god they made this vow to remains a point of bitter contention among the devout, but their pendant's power - and limitations - are irrefutable.

Crafted from the tanned, smooth hide of a Western Skyshark, these slippers are astonishingly comfortable. They lack the protective benefits of a good pair of boots, but they can get their wearers out of almost any bind.
A plain iron lance, imbued with supernatural gravitas via the artifice of the mage Gell. It strikes with a force many times stronger than that imparted by the wielder.

An ancient artefact of Okawaru, these woolen robes were lost when a former champion failed a duel. Its enchantments increase in power when the wearer emerges victorious from threatening combat, but resorting to the use of scrolls or potions for assistance causes them to fade away again.

A disc of crackling metal, created by a woman whose cunning artifice and crafty politics once united a continent. Most of her surviving inventions are closely guarded by various royals, ostensible proof of their claim to be her true successor, but this early prototype slipped through their fingers.

Hand cannons use magical dust to launch projectiles. The alchemists who craft them boast of their potency, but omit the smoke and noise blasted out with each shot. Filled with powdered blastmotes, Mule packs an especially powerful kick.

A pair of suede gloves covered in a dizzying array of delicate sigils. While originally intended to aid in the crafting of magical devices, they are nonetheless useful for wringing every last drop of power out of someone else's work.

This orb is the work of a master artificer, contracted to retrieve the orb, who valued their life more than their professional integrity. While this fake faithfully recreates the eerie glow and space-warping properties of the true orb, the power it grants is artificial and only accessible to skilled evokers.

A gleaming breastplate with a slot in its centre for a holy symbol or bejewelled coat of arms. Those who hear commands given by its wearer feel filled with the power to carry them out, no matter the adversity.

The skull of a legendary necromancer, seemingly parted from the rest of its body. When held, it seems disinclined to explain the precise circumstances of its ending up in this state, but offers no objection to others siphoning what considerable necromantic power still remains in its ancient bones.

The handiwork of a mad mycologist who once attempted to overcome the genetic anxiety of wandering mushrooms by cultivating a species that could be easily transported without disturbing them. The result is as much a living organism as it is a piece of clothing, every linen fibre twined together with fungal mycelia that draw both nutrients and confidence from whoever wears it. And in exchange for such trifles as blood or peptides, the colony will instinctively lash out to defend its wearer from whatever they perceive as a threat. It's like wearing a thousand tiny friends at once! And the humming they fill your mind with in the dark is actually quite lulling.... (This item also occupies your helmet slot.)

An extravagant crown of gold filigree and glittering jewels that even a king could feel immodest wearing. It grants its wearer a regal aura the match of any in heaven and also a great deal of unearned confidence.

A large pair of ghostly claws fashioned into gloves by a fenstrider coven for use in necromantic rites. The magically inclined and pugilistically favoured alike may grasp their connection with the spirits of the dead, but these pincers make grasping anything else an exercise in frustration. (This item prohibits the use of a weapon or shield while equipped.)

A flamboyant suit of ancient armour that has led to many minor schisms between historians, as it is uncertain whether it was made from some renowned witch's pet dragon, or her frequent prey, or from her own non-human body itself. Regardless of its origins, the magic woven into it freely rains toxins all over its bearer's especially misfortunate foes.

An instrument of terror crafted by some of Qazlal's most infamous prophets, meant to coax forth a three-year winter preceding the end of time. Those chilled by its wielder will feel fate's icy grip upon their throat. As with all athames, blows made with it against those suffering baleful negative statuses (other than poison) have increased base damage.

The resonating scales of the great fire-breathing dragon Zmysua, an ancient occultist fond of debilitation and devastation. Her loving rivalry with the elder dragon arcanist Yntzoia was legendarily destructive, and led to the both of them seeking out endless mystic augmentations to triumph over one another- even now, these scales still hum with thirst to confront what remains of their opposite beyond death.

The thrumming scales of the great frost-breathing dragon Yntzoia, an ancient arcanist fond of spectacle and destruction. Her tumultous relationship with the elder dragon occultist Zmysua was quite infamous, and led to the both of them seeking out endless mystic augmentations seeking more time for reconciliation- even now, these scales still reverberate with hunger to return to what remains of their opposite beyond death.
Even the trolls have their share of nature poets, glassy-eyed dreamers, and starving artists. This is the masterwork of one such restless soul, a paean to the heavens far above.

A massive polearm hewn in one piece from a coolibah tree. Its blade is no less sharp for being made of wood, and those caught in its enchanted branches will soon find themselves at home in the bog from which this deadly weapon sprouted.

The staff of a venerable master monk who drove away her foes as easily as her attachments and (so the legend says) eventually transcended life and death altogether. A worthy wielder may unlock the staff's great potential, provided they follow its former owner's peculiar ideas of balance and comportment.

An unassuming sword resembling a prop weapon for theatrical use. But behold! A twist here, a press there, and the real blade springs forth; glittering, wicked, murderous. Has it killed before? If so, it left no witnesses. Shall it kill for you? If you're sly enough, it will do just as you like.

The favored sword of one of the battlemage Yara's most illustrious pupils, an alleged demigoddess who often boasted that one spell and one slash were enough to settle any battle. Indeed, all of her duels ended in just such a fashion, including her last.

A truly ancient set of armour designed for maximum protection and flexibility. Evidently intended for use by mounted hexslingers, its magic wards and sigils are in a hopeless state of disrepair. Nevertheless, some traces of their power still remain.

The half-stitched, or half-unstitched, torso of a bone dragon, fashioned (if one may call it that) into a truly wretched piece of armour. Its jagged bones seem to pulse with unlife, awaiting the command of some unholy master.

A bronze chestpiece of masterful make. It is etched all over with religious imagery, but the focus of the scene is obscured by a great dark stain {{ if you.can_smell() then return "that smells strongly " end }}of ashes and salt. It seems somehow blasphemous to wear.
